findings.text: 把官方DSH Web界面经配对交给自有手机/电脑操作，管理设备会话与入口状态；配对是完整主机控制，不是只读分享或工作区隔离。见[Q01](#research-q01)。
QR窗口token→单次grant→活设备cookie/header/query→先鉴权再环回代理，附Host自身内层cookie并重塑同源；官方shell/客户端rewrite复用。见[Q02](#research-q02)。

本子包manifest/bundle、host/client实际入口、token/grant/store、pair控制与官方shell、remote HTTP/WS/inner auth/header、权限/退出、LAN plan/forward/firewall caller、默认relay claim/bridge和tunnel/ingress控制入口、posture/遥测；同固定SSH routes/protocol/loopback/registry/engine/PTY仅条件组合。未全审实际宿主所有权限/事件/凭据、TLS/密码学、云端relay/Cloudflare与全部binary/进程清理、移动CSS/Service Worker/浏览器兼容，不执行目标。
@linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui 0.4.12，Apache-2.0，DSH>=0.2.1-rc.3、Node ^22.19或>=24、host/client和bundle。未安装/网络验收；one-time描述须区分可复用QR窗口token和真正单次grant。
常驻Host/转发/长流、可选边缘、设备/升级和分通道恢复人工未知；默认relay与遥测是外联条件，不能按扫码或stop数算收益。表见[Q05](#research-q05)。

仅自有受控设备、无敏感数据的独立可弃置实例，在加载前显式relay=false/autoTunnel=false/ingressSync=false且清不需的公网token/base，现场保留本机操作者和停Host/断网手段，先做受控LAN小样。核未配对拒绝、新HTTP/新WS、撤销后旧mux后续消息、store/重启及既有宿主凭据，不能把配对/心跳或stop状态当全部退出。身份/通道/任务或资源不明立即停用并人工切断核查，硬即时撤销、只读多用户与生产凭据统一控制需求先观察。见[Q05](#research-q05)。
官方界面复用、新入口配对/门禁及局部部署清理有源码；手机实际可用、净省时与统一撤销/工作停止未证。效果表见[Q05](#research-q05)。
可借鉴先设备gate后内层cookie、grant consume再liveness、持久撤销失败删旧表及保留forward身份；rawpipe/其他凭据/布尔probe的边界须显式，不能把单点fail-closed泛化。见[Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)。
把官方界面配对交接、新请求设备门禁和部署状态接为跨设备入口，grant与持久撤销fallback有实际机制；非新Agent/多租户安全。见[Q01](#research-q01)、[Q02](#research-q02)。
旧WS rawpipe可在撤销后继续承载新消息，不能只称在途HTTP；三路径deny不等宿主全部方法/凭据隔离。同版SSH启用时受配对代理可重塑loopback进入其路由/PTY，局部门卫非跨插件隔离。见[Q03](#research-q03)。
先验证设备绑定连接关闭与分通道退出回执、probe未知状态细化；既有posture/撤销机制保留，简单原组件修复/人工清单够用就否定独立产品。见[Q06](#research-q06)。
兼容宿主/Node、可信设备/实例/网络、正确LAN和状态写权限必需；relay等外部模式分开，SSH仅条件组合，非Remote启动前提。表见[Q05](#research-q05)。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)成熟Web/代理上界面整合novelty小幅9，仍是成熟受控远程机制的界面/入口组合，未到清晰方法差异18；[Q02](#research-q02)token/grant、设备gate与内层认证/持久fallback形成明确局部机制15，超薄接线8，但[Q03](#research-q03)非统一退出正确性23；鉴权先行与通道分层可条件迁移10，宿主/浏览器约束未到普适15；[Q05](#research-q05)界面复用简化8，仍有网络/权限和退出人工，未到11。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)接续原DSH工作主要入口便利workflow9，未改分工18；[Q02](#research-q02)配对交接/设备状态使delivery小幅8，非已验跨设备业务/退出交付15；[Q01](#research-q01)同官方实例扩到手机/另一电脑使reach10，超仅桌面便利5，真实可用/新群体未测不到15；[Q04](#research-q04)复用同Host/界面与可选统一relay交接改变远程服务/资源安排，经济小幅4，但不把外部平台全归本包、托管及恢复责任仍重，未到8；TCO/节时未知另记，非实测收益。

recommendation.reason: 有跨设备接续需要且只用自有受控设备的用户，可在无敏感数据的独立测试实例、加载前显式关闭relay/隧道/同步和不需的公网配置，保留现场本机操作者/停Host或断网手段后试受控LAN。它复用官方界面并在新HTTP/WS握手先验设备，但旧mux不逐帧撤销、宿主其他凭据/任务和公网信任仍须分层核对，局部loopback不是组合隔离。身份/入口/旧流或工作状态不明就停止扩用并人工切断验证，要求即时硬撤所有通道、只读多租户或生产凭据统一撤销者先观察。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)自有设备接续同实例及授权/退出验收具体，超泛远程便利15；需求频次/实际收益未测，未到30。

advantage.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)官方UI复用、grant/设备gate超简单开放端口6；[Q03](#research-q03)、[Q04](#research-q04)退出/凭据/网络仍重，未替代成熟受控方案到19。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)到[Q04](#research-q04)真实caller/状态/代理/退出反证及同版SSH组合原文超README片段6；未运行端到端/旧流/手机/公网实验，未到19。

cost.rationale: [Q05](#research-q05)独立无敏感实例、自有设备与物理停Host手段给可控小样，超0不可接受；[Q03](#research-q03)旧流/其他凭据与[Q04](#research-q04)默认外联/监听/三方信任使恢复负担重、TCO未知，未到10。

publication.summaries.text: DSH远程界面插件，让自有手机或电脑配对后操作同一官方Web实例，提供设备会话、移动适配和LAN/可选公网入口。

items.界面: 官方Web shell跨设备复用、移动适配与本机配对/状态入口
items.Host 路由: 设备门禁的HTTP/WS环回代理及pair控制面
items.后台: 设备持久/失效、LAN边缘与可选relay/tunnel控制和posture探测

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 用途 | 条件与边界 |
|---|---|---|
| 配对/会话 | 窗口QR、一次grant、活设备表 | 广泛Host控制，非物理设备/工作区隔离 |
| 官方远程界面 | 手机/电脑同实例、同源重写 | 实际浏览器/SDK兼容未验 |
| HTTP/WS代理 | 鉴权后借内层cookie重发 | 旧WS不是逐帧鉴权；deny仅三路径前缀 |
| LAN/公网入口 | loopback边缘、可选relay/Cloudflare | relay默认true；TLS/三方信任和清理另核 |
| 状态/撤销 | 设备表/失效/探针与关闭caller | 不是所有凭据、长流和工作负载统一退出 |

publication.advice.text: 仅自有受控设备、无敏感数据的独立可弃置实例，在加载前显式relay=false/autoTunnel=false/ingressSync=false且清不需的公网token/base，现场保留本机操作者和停Host/断网手段，先做受控LAN小样。核未配对拒绝、新HTTP/新WS、撤销后旧mux后续消息、store/重启及既有宿主凭据，不能把配对/心跳或stop状态当全部退出。身份/通道/任务或资源不明立即停用并人工切断核查，硬即时撤销、只读多用户与生产凭据统一控制需求先观察。见[Q05](#research-q05)。

      "path": "packages/dsh-remote-web-ui/README.md",
      "content": "# dsh-remote-web-ui · Mobile & Cross-Device Remote Web Control for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)\n\nEnglish | [中文](README.zh.md)\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-remote-web-ui?style=flat-square\" alt=\"Version\">\n   \n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%3E%3D0.2.1--rc.3-4c6ef5?style=flat-square&labelColor=454a54\" alt=\"DSH\">\n   \n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue?style=flat-square\" alt=\"License\">\n</p>\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <strong>Mobile & Cross-Device Remote Web Control for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)</strong><br>\n  <em>Instant QR Pairing · Cross-Device PC Access · Mobile Touch Gestures · Cloudflare Tunnels · Secure Device Session</em>\n</p>\n\n> Seamless remote access for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI and desktop client sharing the **exact same interface**: pair an iPhone, Android smartphone, tablet, or another computer from the QR code next to settings. Both ends run the authentic official Web GUI — phones receive an injected portrait touch layer while remote computers enjoy the complete desktop workbench. Access is guarded by expiring pairing tokens and revocable sessions. Built-in LAN binding and optional Cloudflare quick tunnels enable effortless external access with persistent hostnames.\n\nThis package is an official external plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH), structured as a cordis bundle: the host half manages pairing tokens, device sessions, `/api/pair` routes, the gated `/remote` channel, and LAN binding; the browser half renders the remote access trigger, QR pairing modal, live device roster, settings card, and mobile portrait touch adaptation.\n\n## What it does\n\n- **Entry**: a phone icon beside the settings button in both the expanded sidebar and the narrow rail; its tooltip and accessible label say \"Remote access\".\n- **Panel**: \"Remote access\" title, a \"Pair a device\" card with the status area (\"Waiting for a device\" + status badge), a large QR code, the pairing link with its copy button, Stop / Refresh QR actions, and the authorized-device roster (a saved device name that falls back to the User-Agent-derived label, online/offline, last active time, per-device rename and unpair, and a merge action for rows sharing one User-Agent). Credential-bearing device ids and raw User-Agent values are never rendered. Both the phone and the PC use the same time-limited link: until it expires or the QR is refreshed, that link can pair several devices, each with its own device session.\n- **Phone side**: scanning the QR binds the phone with a time-limited token and reloads into the **official Web GUI** — there is no second interface to drift from. While the phone is in portrait, the plugin injects a touch-adaptation layer over the running UI (see \"The mobile adaptation layer\" below). The accept chain is cookieless (`/pair-accept` → `/pair-app`): the plugin itself serves the official shell, so the phone needs no harness browser-auth cookie at all. A reopen service worker (https origins) then owns later navigations to `/` from history, bookmarks, or tab restore, so the phone reopens straight into the app instead of a 401 dead end (see Security model).\n- **PC side**: the same link opens the full desktop Web GUI on another computer over the gated `/remote` channel; unpaired PCs see a guided blocking page (with a manual pair-token input) and no workspace data behind it.\n- **Security**: one active token at a time (a refresh invalidates the old link; the link stays re-usable within its expiry window so a scan handed between browsers can complete pairing; it expires). 停止 revokes every paired device and the current token — the `/remote` channel cuts them off on their next request. Pairing is this plugin's access control for the `/remote` channel; the web server keeps its loopback bind, so a LAN browser reaches the app through this plugin's gated `/remote` gateway (the client moves its transport there) rather than the native `/api`, which the harness Host fence answers with 403 for a LAN authority (see Security model). Loopback (127.0.0.1) keeps using `/api` directly, and so does a page an application on this machine delivered — the desktop shell's `dsh-app://app/` or a `file:` page — because a pairing link is reachable only over the network. A paired device is a **full-control credential** (see Security model).\n- **LAN access toggle (runtime forwarder)**: the settings card starts a forwarder instead of touching any file. The web server keeps its loopback bind, and the forwarder listens on this machine's LAN IPv4 address at the same port, re-issuing every request — HTTP and WebSocket upgrades alike — to `127.0.0.1:<port>`. `--host`/`--port` keep their ordinary meaning, so an explicit `dsh web --host <a LAN address>` still works and the forwarder then yields the port. The toggle applies while the process runs: no restart, no profile edit. When this machine has no LAN IPv4 address the forwarder stays off and the card says so. It maintains the matching host firewall rule (Windows Defender via netsh; Linux firewalld/ufw/iptables; other platforms report the firewall as unmanaged) and shows the live bind, the reachable LAN URLs, the forwarder state (`forward { listening, host, port, reason, error }`) beside the host's own `localBindHost`, and the firewall state.\n- **Live status**: the desktop badge flips to 已连接 in real time; an `/api` posture probe reports any host whose `/api` fence the SDK leaves open, and the auto-tunnel state appears on the panel while the tunnel is starting.\n- **Self-update lives next door**: the one-click family update is its own plugin (`dsh-update`, the same sidebar foot seat), so turning remote access off — or disabling this plugin — never removes the update trigger.\n- **Desktop foot row**: on the wide sidebar the footer-action occupants share the official Settings trigger's line instead of stacking above it, so no single control owns a full-width row; any other foot block (the usage glance card, another plugin's) keeps a full row above them, and the 56px rail keeps the shell's stacked foot.\n\n## The mobile adaptation layer\n\nThe official desktop layout already auto-collapses the sidebar below 1024px. On top of that, while the viewport is portrait + coarse pointer + narrower than 1100px the plugin injects:\n\n- a CSS sheet keyed on CSS-Modules **semantic suffixes** (`[class$=\"_composerSeat\"]`) so the selectors survive official rebuilds that only change hashes: 44px touch targets on the collapsed rail, 16px inputs (prevents iOS focus zoom), safe-area padding for the composer, compact type for the message list and sidebar, a column layout for the settings modal, and a full-width PlanReview card;\n- a **draggable whale button** as the entry to the collapsed sidebar (position persisted; wired to the official `ctx.layout.toggleSidebar()`), hidden while the sidebar is expanded;\n- **gestures**: left-swipe collapses the sidebar, right-swipe in the conversation opens it; long-pressing a session row opens the same action menu as the desktop ellipsis; tapping a session row or anywhere outside the sidebar collapses it again;\n- **input behavior for touch**: Enter only inserts a newline (send goes through the send button), programmatic composer focus is suppressed (no spurious keyboards), and official tooltip bubbles are hidden because taps leave them stuck;\n- **mobile plugin scope**: while the layer is active, the right-hand details column and the desktop-oriented tool surfaces (SSH terminal, skill explorer, task board, git graph, pet, usage) are hidden - keyed on the L2 semantic roots (`data-dsh-plugin`), so ownership stays with the declaring plugin and class churn cannot resurrect them. These are render suppressions; the client bundles still load. Activation also closes the details panel through the official `ctx.layout.closeDetails()`.\n- a **manual opt-out**: `sessionStorage.dsh-remote-force-desktop = 1` disables the whole layer; landscape, desktop, and wide viewports are never touched.\n\nThe paired remote desktop also runs in **host mode**: on this harness line the \"configuration plane is local\" behavior is a client-side branch on `connection.isLoopback`, and the channel boot script installs the transport hook (`__DSH_TRANSPORT__.ownsHost = true`) before any boot entry. Host mode is **server-granted**: the hook is installed only when the device-gated app landing (`/pair-app`) published the grant marker ahead of the boot patch, so a shell served to an unpaired browser — a fence-open deployment — never poses as the machine owner. Settings, credentials, agent presets, and deliverables therefore work on the phone exactly as on the desktop — every call still rides the gated `/remote` channel. Three control planes stay physically local: `/api/pair/*`, `/api/update/*`, and `/api/plugin-manager/*`.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- A DSH installation whose `dsh` CLI supports profiles (`dsh --profile`, `dsh plugin`) — the profile/bundle mechanism this package rides on.\n- For LAN use, either flip the **局域网访问** toggle in the settings card — it listens at once on this machine's current LAN IPv4 address at the web server's port, so after a network change flip it off and on again — or start with `dsh web --host <a LAN address of this machine>`. A wildcard `--host 0.0.0.0` works only on a host that still accepts it; DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 and later refuses it outright. With the default `127.0.0.1` bind the panel shows an explicit explanation instead of a dead QR code — unless a public base URL is configured (see \"Remote access over the internet\" below), which makes the QR reachable from anywhere without rebinding, after which a phone on the same network is moved off the tunnel onto the LAN origin by the landing page. The panel's mint/stop endpoints are loopback-only by design: a desktop browser opened at the LAN URL sees a \"配对面板仅限本机使用\" banner.\n- For the one-click public tunnel (`autoTunnel`), the `cloudflared` platform binary ships with the package (its postinstall downloads it; a runtime download covers installers that skip postinstall scripts). No user-side tooling, account, or domain is needed.\n- The same binary also powers the fixed-hostname named-tunnel mode (`tunnelToken`): the public hostname never changes, so a paired phone keeps its bookmark and its pairing cookie across restarts and never re-pairs.\n\n## Install\n\nInstall the family aggregate package `@linxin666/dsh-web-all` (all plugins and skins in one) or this plugin alone:\n\n```sh\n# Recommended: install directly from npm\ndsh plugin --profile web add @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui@latest\n\n# Or from the repository (development loop)\ngit clone https://github.com/zhu1090093659/dsh-web.git\ncd dsh-web\npnpm install && pnpm -r build\ndsh plugin --profile web add link:$(pwd)/packages/dsh-remote-web-ui\n```\n\nRestart the profile (`dsh web`), then open the phone icon in the sidebar foot. The plugin's `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the single plugin row that mounts both halves.\n\n> `github:<org>/<repo>` installs work for a standalone repo whose package sits at the root (the `prepare` script builds `lib/` during install; pnpm ≥10 blocks that until you copy the printed key into the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `allowBuilds` and re-run). Monorepo subpackages use the `link:` form above.\n\n## Use\n\n1. Open the settings card (设置 → Web 插件 → 远程访问) and flip **局域网访问** on; the card shows the live bind, the forwarder state beside the host's own `localBindHost`, the firewall state, and the reachable LAN URLs, and it says why the LAN entry is off when this machine has no LAN address. The forwarder starts and stops at once, with no restart: after a network change, flip the toggle off and on again so it follows the machine's new address.\n2. Start `dsh web`, click the phone icon, and the panel mints a fresh time-limited QR.\n3. Scan with the phone (or open the copied link): the device pairs and boots the **official Web GUI** served cookieless by the plugin (`/pair-accept` → `/pair-app`), which reloads into `/`. When the link names the public base, the landing page also probes the advertised LAN origins (one short no-cors request to `/pair-ping` per candidate) and moves the phone to the first one that answers, remembering the decision for the session: the public page it was served from stays usable throughout, so the probe never blocks pairing, and a phone that is not on that network simply stays where it is. On a phone, the portrait adaptation layer is already active — same layout as the desktop, same live state. Later reopens from history or a bookmark go straight back into the app (https origins; see Security model).\n4. **To pair a PC instead**: copy the same link and open it in a browser on the other computer. After the same round trip the full Web GUI runs there over the gated `/remote` channel; unpaired PCs see the guided blocking page and no data. One active token pairs one device; mint a fresh QR for the next device.\n5. The desktop badge flips to 已连接 in real time; the device roster lists the paired devices with per-device 取消配对, and 停止 revokes everything.\n6. Configure pairing lifetime, device limits, the LAN fence policy (`requirePairingForLan`), the public base URL, the auto tunnel, the stable-hostname relay, and the named-tunnel token in the same settings card. Which network the pair traverses needs no choice: the QR link names the public base and the landing page moves a same-network phone to a LAN origin by itself. If that probe ever misjudges, pin it with the patch-only `pairingSource` key (`auto` | `public` | `lan`); the card carries no control for it, so a save from the card leaves it alone.\n\n## Remote access over the internet (tunnels)\n\nA tunnel process restart — most often a mobile network dropping and reconnecting — used to drop the public host from the pairing fence the moment the tunnel left `running`, so the address still printed in the QR code answered 403, including on the deliberately public `/api/pair/status` (issue #1547). A named tunnel's fixed hostname and a registered relay origin never change, so both now stay trusted throughout the reconnect; a quick tunnel's previous host stays trusted for a 60 s grace window, because the edge may still be delivering a connection the phone already opened, and is dropped only if the tunnel has not come back by then.\n\n### One-click public tunnel (recommended)\n\nSet **自动公网隧道** (autoTunnel) in the settings card. The plugin runs its own Cloudflare quick tunnel (`cloudflared` ships with the package), feeds the minted public URL into the QR base and the pairing fence dynamically, and keeps the posture probe informed — a phone anywhere can pair at any time. The manual public address and the named-tunnel token below are ignored while this is on. The minted hostname is ephemeral and changes on every `dsh web` restart — the stable-hostname relay below keeps the phone's origin fixed across those restarts. A host that dies without tearing its tunnel down leaves the `cloudflared` child running, so each start reaps the child it recorded (pid plus an exactly matching command line) and never a process it did not start itself.\n\n### Stable-hostname relay (default on; pair once across restarts)\n\nWhile the quick tunnel runs, the plugin additionally registers its current tunnel URL with the dsh-market relay registry and rebuilds the QR on a fixed origin — `https://<id>.dsh-market.com` — minted once per profile and stored under `$DSH_HOME/remote-web-ui-registry/`. The hostname never changes, so the phone's bookmark and its pairing cookie keep working across `dsh web` restarts with no Cloudflare account, no dashboard, and no domain of your own.\n\n- Registration is secret-authenticated: the plugin mints a 256-bit secret next to the identity and re-syncs the mapping on every tunnel start (crash restarts included) with capped backoff. If the registry is unreachable, the QR falls back to the raw quick URL for that session and the panel says so.\n- A phone opening the stable origin while the instance is offline sees an explicit \"instance offline — refresh in a moment, no re-pairing needed\" page instead of a dead link.\n- Turn **固定域名中继** (relay) off in the settings card to keep the deployment entirely on the ephemeral origin; the registry row is removed at once. Trust note: relayed traffic transits the dsh-market edge (a Cloudflare Worker operated by the package author) — see Security model.\n- The relay control plane is additive: whenever the relay is on and the web server port is bound, the plugin claims a named-tunnel lease from `https://dsh-market.com/api/relay/claim` — the worker finds or creates the tunnel named `dsh-relay-<id>`, writes its ingress (catch-all rule included) and an exact proxied CNAME, and hands back that instance's own tunnel token. A lease an operator flipped to the bridge transport converges nothing in the account: that claim creates no tunnel, no ingress and no CNAME, sends no Cloudflare API call at all, keeps only the hostname and the bridge grant, and answers no `tunnel` block — the bridge's data plane is the instance's own Durable Object, so there is nothing to build and nothing to count against the account's 1 000-tunnel quota. The plugin then runs a named connector on the same hostname beside the quick connector; the `mode` the control plane answers names the one the phone is served from, so neither the switch nor its rollback needs a plugin restart. A failed claim is not fatal: the quick tunnel and the origin the registry already gave the phone keep serving, and the claim retries with capped backoff (`502` carries `retryAfterMs`). Turning the toggle off only `release`s the lease (the tunnel and the DNS record stay, so re-enabling is instant); only an explicit `retire` or the 90-day idle cron recovers the source.\n- The bridge transport rides the same lease: the plugin dials `wss://dsh-market.com/api/relay/bridge?id=<id>` with the lease secret in the `Authorization` header and serves every bridged request and phone WebSocket from that one socket, forwarding the public origin as `Host` and never the loopback authority it dials. It idles while the control plane answers `mode=quick`; with no connector attached the Worker falls back to the quick path inside the same request and marks the answer `x-relay-fallback: no-connector`. Because the claim is the only answer that carries the bridge grant, it does not wait for a quick tunnel: an instance served over the bridge reaches its object with `autoTunnel` off. The connector keeps its state in `$DSH_HOME/remote-web-ui-relay-bridge.json` — state, instance, endpoint, local upstream and the last dial error — so a connector that never attached is readable without the host log.\n\n### Fixed-hostname named tunnel (bring your own domain)\n\nThe relay above already fixes the phone's origin on a shared dsh-market subdomain. A Cloudflare named tunnel is the alternative for deployments that want a hostname on **their own** domain: its public hostname is permanent, so the phone's bookmark and its pairing cookie keep working across `dsh web` restarts — pair once, never again (until the session idles past `idleExpireMs`).\n\n1. In the Cloudflare dashboard create a Tunnel and map a public hostname — e.g. `dsh.example.com` — to `http://127.0.0.1:3080` (the port `dsh web` listens on).\n2. Copy the tunnel's token and paste it into **固定域名隧道令牌** (tunnelToken) in the settings card.\n3. Set the same hostname as **公网地址** (publicBaseUrl). The token does not carry the hostname, so without this step the tunnel stays off and a warning names the missing piece.\n\nThe plugin then runs `cloudflared tunnel run --token` with the same lifecycle management as the quick tunnel: the binary ships with the package, unexpected exits restart with backoff, a running tunnel's public URL is probed every 60 s and two consecutive failures mint a fresh tunnel through that same restart path, and the posture probe audits the `/api` fence for the fixed host. The token is stored as a settings secret and read back redacted. The auto quick tunnel takes precedence while it is on.\n\nA `running` tunnel is not a terminal state: a connector that lost its Cloudflare edge registration keeps its process and its metrics port alive while the minted hostname stops resolving, so the plugin used to report `running` indefinitely and the relay kept forwarding the phone to the dead address (Cloudflare 530 / Error 1016) instead of the relay's offline page (issue #1723). The readiness watchdog now treats a public URL that stops answering — DNS failure, refused connection, or a Cloudflare 5xx such as 530 — as a dead tunnel after two consecutive probes, and the ordinary backoff restart mints a new URL and re-registers the relay. An unauthenticated `401`/`403` answer still counts as alive, because that is a healthy round trip to a harness that has not been paired yet.\n\n#### Keeping the ingress port in sync (optional, update-only)\n\nA named tunnel's hostname is permanent, but its ingress rule names a fixed local port (`http://127.0.0.1:3080` above). When `dsh web` later listens on another port — an operator `--port`, another profile, a second instance on the old one — the hostname still resolves and answers 502 while everything in this plugin still believes the address is published. Turn on **Cloudflare config sync** (`ingressSync`) with an account-level API token (`cfApiToken`), the `cfAccountId` and the `cfTunnelId`, and the plugin keeps that one number following the port it actually bound:\n\n- one read on start; the document is written only when the matched rule's service has drifted from the bound port;\n- only the `service` of the rule whose hostname exactly equals `publicBaseUrl`'s host is touched — one full-document PUT, because the API has no single-rule patch, with every other rule and every top-level key proven identical first;\n- a document it cannot prove that about is reported and never written: a missing or duplicated hostname, a wildcard anywhere, an `ingress` that is not an array, a missing catch-all, a service that is not an http(s) origin, or a service hosted anywhere but on this machine — only loopback literals (127.0.0.0/8, `::1`, `localhost`) and this host's own LAN addresses are retargeted, so a neighbour's address or a DNS name is never touched. No rule is added and no catch-all is invented;\n- the write is read back once. A disagreement is a conflict and stops there: one tunnel document has one writer, so a deployment whose dashboard or another sync owns it is reconciled by hand;\n- the bound port is the target: before the listener binds nothing is requested (the same settle re-plan that starts the quick tunnel delivers it), and the tunnel token's own format is never parsed.\n\nThe state frame reports `off`/`waiting`/`applied`/`failed`/`conflict` with the hostname, the port, the two service strings and the reason, and the settings card renders it beside the switch. The quick tunnel takes precedence: with `autoTunnel` on there is no named tunnel to update and the sync reads as off.\n\n### Manual tunnels (bring your own)\n\nExpose the local port with any tunnel and set **公网地址** (publicBaseUrl), e.g.:\n\n```sh\n# 1. Expose the local port (whatever dsh web is listening on):\ncloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:3080\n#    prints something like: https://xxxx-xxxx-xxxx.trycloudflare.com\n\n# 2. Start dsh web as usual. Do not add --trusted-host for the tunnel\n#    domain unless you intentionally want the SDK to trust that host for\n#    /api. Keep the LAN bind off if only tunnel access is wanted.\n```\n\nThen set the printed URL as 公网地址. The QR link is built from it, and the plugin's pairing fence accepts the tunneled authority. The posture probe keeps auditing which `/api` authorities the SDK fence leaves open.\n\n## Development\n\nWork from this repository (no sibling checkout needed):\n\n```sh\ncd dsh-web\nexport NPM_TOKEN='<token>'   # only if private @deepseek-ai auth is still required\npnpm install\npnpm --filter @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui run build\npnpm --filter @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui test\npnpm --filter @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui run typecheck\n```\n\nThe peer APIs come from the official NPM SDK: every `@deepseek-ai/*` package used here is declared in devDependencies (0.2.1-rc.3 cohort), and TypeScript/Vitest resolve types straight from node_modules — no DSH source checkout is required. The consumer-side `prepare` build (`tsdown.prepare.config.ts`) transpiles without type checking, so git installs work without any harness checkout either.\n\n## Checks\n\n```sh\npnpm run typecheck\npnpm test\npnpm run build\n```\n\n## Harness contract dependencies\n\nPinned to the 0.2.1-rc.3 line; the seams this build relies on:\n\n- **`sidebar.footer.action` foot seat** (the 0.1.7 shell composition): the sidebar declares and renders the seat the remote entry occupies.\n- **`ctx.layout.toggleSidebar()`** (packages/client/ui-layout): the whale button expands the collapsed sidebar through the official panel-action face.\n- **`ctx.connection.authenticatedUrl()`** (packages/client/connection): the sanctioned launch-token seam the proxy redeems once for its inner credential (`src/inner-auth.ts`), so re-issued `/api` calls satisfy the harness browser-auth check.\n- **`__DSH_FILE_UPLOAD__`** (file-upload client hooks): the optional pre-Cordis transport the upload service reads once at construction. The remote boot patch publishes it so background uploads stay on the rewritten main-thread fetch instead of a Web Worker that escapes the channel (issue #1580).\n- **`__DSH_TRANSPORT__.ownsHost`** (client-connection transport hooks): the host-mode flip for paired remote desktops. It is installed only when the device-gated app landing published the `__DSH_REMOTE_HOST_GRANT__` marker ahead of the boot patch, so the flip is server-granted rather than asserted from the origin. There is no host-side per-method privilege pin on this line — the configuration plane branches on `connection.isLoopback` in the client — and no `api/gate` waterfall either (the gate listener stays mounted for deployments that gain the seam; pairing enforcement lives on this plugin's own `/remote` channel).\n- **Web server bind ownership**: the profile's `- id: webserver` row belongs to the official bundle and this plugin never writes it — same-id patch rows replace a row's config wholesale, and the user patch layer cannot evaluate `webStartup`-dependent `!!js` expressions reliably, so the row keeps `host: !!js ctx.webStartup.host ?? '127.0.0.1'` and `--host`/`--port` reach it. LAN reachability is runtime state instead: the forwarder in `src/lan-forward.ts` listens on the LAN interface at the web server's actual port and re-issues to `127.0.0.1` on the same port.\n\nThe fence helpers (`isTrustedApiRequest` / `isLoopbackHostname`) are reimplemented locally in `src/gate.ts` / `src/routes.ts`: the connection plugin stopped exporting them, so the pairing routes carry their own copy scoped to the literals the QR links advertise. The loopback question is split in two there: `isLoopbackUpstream` (loopback socket and Host, forwarding headers ignored) only decides whether a Host can be answered at all, while `isLoopbackClient` (no forwarding header) decides who receives a credential or the desktop payload. The shared copy in `shared/host/loopback.ts` keeps `isLoopbackRequest` refusing every forwarded request and adds `isForwardedLoopbackRequest` for the narrower shape a route family may admit behind its own default-off switch.\n\n## Manual E2E: LAN pairing round trip\n\nThe unit/component specs cover the route family, the gate, the channel, the LAN forwarder with its status frame, and the adaptation layer, but the pairing loop involves a real browser on a non-loopback origin. Repeat this after any change to the wire contract or the connection loop:\n\n1. Start an isolated instance: `DSH_HOME=/tmp/dsh-qa dsh --profile web --no-open --port 3191`; open the card at `http://127.0.0.1:3191`, flip **局域网访问** on, and confirm the card reports the forwarder listening on the machine's LAN IPv4 at 3191.\n2. Open the **loopback** URL (`http://127.0.0.1:3191`) in a browser: the phone icon sits in the sidebar foot; the panel mints a QR whose link is `<lan-url>/pair-accept?pair=<token>`. With a public base configured the link names that origin instead — reachable from anywhere — and the landing does the network choice described under **Use**.\n3. In a second tab under mobile emulation (390x844, touch) open that link: the chain `/pair-accept → /pair-app?grant=<one-time> → /` on an https origin, ending at `/pair-app` instead over plain-HTTP LAN, sets the device cookie, spends the grant, serves the patched official shell, and boots the UI — `document.body.classList` carries `dsh-remote-portrait`, the adaptation stylesheet and the whale button exist, and `__DSH_TRANSPORT__.ownsHost` is `true`. The settings surface renders host data (host mode), not a memory mirror. In an https deployment the shell also registers the reopen service worker (`/pair-app.sw.js`); reloading `/` in that tab boots the app instead of the harness 401. Over plain-HTTP LAN the same tab reloads `/pair-app` and boots the app from the pairing cookie instead.\n4. The desktop badge flips to 已连接 in real time; a LAN-origin desktop page instead shows the 配对面板仅限本机使用 banner and opens no status stream.\n5. 停止 on the desktop cuts the device off: its next request 403s with `unpaired` (the fence page offers the manual pair-token input).\n\nThe public path is the same round trip through a tunnel (see \"Remote access over the internet\"): loopback mint → device opens the public QR URL → accept → official UI, and when the advertised LAN origin actually answers (check with `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://<lan-ip>:<port>/pair-ping`, expecting 204) the landing replaces itself with `http://<lan-ip>:<port>/pair-app?grant=<one-time>` and the UI boots from the LAN origin. Re-scanning the public QR within the same session lands on the public source again, because the decision records the failed switch. Only `publicBaseUrl` (plugin config) names the tunneled host; `--trusted-host` is not part of this pairing flow. 快速上手：一行命令通过 npm 或 GitHub 仓库地址直接安装 | [插件安装快速上手](#快速上手) |\n\n## 官方桌面客户端\n\n对于希望直接使用独立桌面应用的用户，推荐下载并使用官方发布的 DeepSeek Harness 桌面客户端（DeepSeek Harness Desktop）。\n\n官方桌面客户端与 `dsh web` 共用 `~/.dsh` 数据目录，其 `@linxin666/dsh-web-all`（或 `@linxin666/dsh-web-all@latest`），点击安装；\n3. 安装完成后重启客户端，即可在客户端中使用任务看板、主题皮肤、远程控制等全套插件能力。\n\n## 创意工坊（dsh-market.com）\n\n[创意工坊](https://dsh-market.com) 是 DSH 生态的一站式资产分发平台，统一提供主题皮肤、桌面宠物、功能插件与社区 Agent 预设。所有项目按照真实设备点赞热度排序，皮肤支持即时试穿预览，插件提供一键安装命令。经典的 Blue Fantasy 蓝色幻想随皮肤插件内置，其余主题皮肤与宠物资产均可在工坊浏览、查看源代码并按需安装。在 Web GUI 的“创意工坊”设置卡中可直接浏览线上清单，皮肤与宠物可一键下载至 DSH 主目录并在对应设置页选用；社区预设下载至本地预设库，启用后即可在“设置 → Agent 预设”中用于新建会话。\n\n![DeepSeek Harness 创意工坊 dsh-market.com — 主题皮肤、桌面宠物与社区插件市场](docs/screenshots/31-market-home.png)\n\n创意工坊站点为本仓库的组成部分：前端为纯静态构建，由构建脚本 `scripts/market-build` 依据 `skin.json`、`pet.json` 与 `community.json` 等数据源自动生成；点赞等动态能力由 Cloudflare Workers 边缘函数与 D1 数据库提供支持（遵循单设备单票限制），代码合入 `main` 分支后自动触发持续集成部署。\n\n创意工坊旨在建立开放透明的社区生态，方便开发者分享作品并让用户自由选择所需扩展。\n\n## 功能插件\n\n### 任务看板（Task Board · 企业级后台长程执行引擎与多 Agent 自动化流水线）\n\n通过侧边栏“任务看板”进入。任务看板不仅仅是一个可视化卡片界面，更是 DeepSeek Harness 官方 Web GUI 与桌面客户端中的**宿主权威后台长程执行与多 Agent 自动化调度引擎**。任务按“待规划、待办、进行中、已完成、已失败”五列进行全生命周期管理，以 Schema v6 事务账本为权威持久化核心，真正实现了长程任务从拆解、分发、团队协作、对抗质检到外部成果闭环的全流程自动化：\n\n- **宿主权威后台驱动与 7x24 小时离线无人值守**：区别于传统仅在前端网页轮询的脆弱看板，所有卡片流转、调度触发与执行监控完全由 DSH 后端 Host 进程作为唯一权威驱动。浏览器仅为异步视图，关闭网页标签页、熄灭屏幕或断开网络，后台智能体会话照常并发执行与原子落盘结算。内置跨平台防休眠电源管理（macOS `caffeinate`、Windows `ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED`、带有 systemd-logind 的 Linux `systemd-inhibit`），允许显示器正常关闭的同时阻止整机因闲置休眠，确保夜间无人值守巡检与流水线准时打卡。\n- **多 Agent 树状级联并发与原生 Agent Teams 团队编排**：复杂工程目标可自由拆解为多层树状子任务（支持 1~3 层深度，内置环路与深度护栏）。**级联执行模式**通过受控准入队列（runLaunchWidth）并发派生多个独立智能体会话，自动跳过已在完成列的子任务，任一子任务失败自适应收拢整树状态；**原生 Agent Teams 模式**深度对接官方团队服务，启动专属 Team Lead 会话并在其内部为每个子任务动态孵化专属 Teammate，协同工具跨智能体联动，实现真正意义上的多智能体团队协同作战。\n- **对抗式双盲质量验收门禁（No False Completion）**：彻底终结 AI 编程中“自述已完成、实则未改动或改崩溃”的虚假交付顽疾。以 goal 形式执行的任务在 Agent 试图调用 `update_goal(complete)` 宣告完工的瞬间被 Host 强制拦截，必须由独立的裁判模型（可自选模型与思考档位）进行真实验收。验收机制沿用严苛的 Coding 质量判据、0.65 绝对通过阈值，每项判据双轮交换 A/B 位置打分消偏，并严格结合会话执行轨迹与宿主工作区真实磁盘文件的 Diff 行级变更审查。首轮未达标精准下发具象结构化问题引导 Agent 自我修复，两次仍不通过才判负，杜绝敷衍糊弄。\n- **全自动 GitHub Issue-to-PR 闭环研发流**：搭配官方扩展（`dsh-client-ui-task-board-github`），实现任务看板与 GitHub Issues / PR 状态的实时双向深度同步。远端 Issue 自动进入看板流水线驱动 Agent 读取需求、定位代码、修复 Bug 并运行测试，验收交付后全自动创建 GitHub Pull Request 并绑定 Issue 关联，PR 合并后自动关闭 Issue，打造全天候无人值守的开源与企业 Issue 自动化修复交付管线。\n- **长程目标驱动、会话持久化与冻结交接包（Freeze Handover）**：任务支持武装内置 `/goal` 引擎进行多轮自主续跑；周期性任务可开启会话复用，保留完整上下文记忆；支持通过 `<<<FREEZE` 协议将会话上下文一键冻结为包含“目标/进度/下一步”的结构化快照，并绑定工作区、预设与权限三元组，接手 Agent 瞬间无缝继承前序成果，同时内置提示词注入防御与来源审计。\n- **企业级权限基线、安全确认门与消费熔断保护**：任务可细粒度钉住工作区、Agent 预设、沙箱权限、执行模型与推理思考强度，钉子校验失败即 Fail-Closed；超出安全基线的高权限操作设有「人工确认门（Permission Gate）」，未在 Web 界面显式放行前坚决拒绝执行与调度，杜绝 Agent 越权危害宿主系统；支持配置看板级每日 Token 消费预算上限（`spendBudgetTokens`），防止后台死循环产生意外费用。\n- **面向智能体的双向工具面与外部成果统一**：向大模型完整暴露 8 个原生工具（`task_board_list`、`task_board_get`、`task_board_create`、`task_board_update`、`task_board_set_parent`、`task_board_run`、`task_board_manage`、`task_board_schedule`），赋予对话中的 Agent 自身查看看板、分解子任务、编排流水线与自动化调度的全套能力；同时支持通过 `record-external-outcome` 统一登记在 Claude Code、Codex 等外部工具中完成的工作，让异构开发流统一汇总至一张看板。\n\n| 多列看板与智能体协作 | 后台定时调度与参数配置 |\n| --- | --- |\n| ![DeepSeek Harness 任务看板界面 — AI 运行时与高效调度引擎）\n\n在新建会话输入框左侧通过专属老虎机拨杆切换，或在“设置 > Agent 预设”中选用。梁神模式（`dsh-liangshen`）是专为追求**极致推理效率、超低静态上下文开销与严苛工程执行纪律**而深度重构的杀手级预设与运行时插件。针对主流大模型在长程编程任务中容易出现的系统提示词冗长膨胀、工具 Schema 挤占上下文、思维链无效空转（如“流水账推理”）以及多轮遗忘退化等痛点，梁神模式通过原生极简提示词、程序化代码工具调用（PTC）、MCP 温和分页与关键事实局部就近投射，提供纯粹而强悍的编程作战体验：\n\n- **极简 Persona 与严苛行动导向纪律（Zero Prompt Waste）**：彻底剥离官方 Standard 预设中冗长繁琐的系统级条文，将提示词极致收敛为单行 Persona 与经过实战千锤百炼的高效工程纪律。内置反思熔断（同一假设推演不超过两轮，缺少事实立即闭合思考并调用原生工具探测，杜绝凭空揣测）、行动导向（思考过程仅用于决定下一步具体操作，严禁在思考中预演完整代码）、并发探索（单轮内并发派发多个独立检测或搜索工具）、YAGNI 与 PDCA 循环（单步验证单一假设，不写冗余注水注释）、以及有界收敛纪律（前置检查最多 2-3 轮即刻收敛，迅速转入实际作答或编辑）。大幅降低静态 Token 占用，让模型注意力百分之百倾注于业务与代码本身。\n- **程序化工具调用传输（PTC · Programmatic Tool Calling）**：彻底终结在每次请求中平铺上百个 JSON Schema 工具参数的低效模式。默认将网络线协议（wire）极致收拢为唯一的 `run_code`（运行 TypeScript 脚本），其余所有工具均通过自动生成的强类型 SDK 在独立的沙箱线程中以代码形式调用。无论系统注册了多少复杂工具，静态传输面始终保持极小体积；模型可原生利用 `Promise.all` 编写并发工具调用，并在程序内预先过滤、聚合、提取关键数据，只将精炼结论回传至对话上下文，从根本上解决大文本输出打爆 Token 的问题。对于习惯原生工具面的场景，亦可在插件设置中一键无缝切换为组装好的原生工具清单（Native）。\n- **MCP 工具温和分页与 LRU 动态激活（Gentle Tool Paging）**：针对海量 MCP 工具或第三方插件扩展，出厂默认启用温和分页（默认匹配 `mcp__*`）。外部工具在初始状态下仅以命名空间摘要形式登记在目录消息中，既不占 wire 协议也不进 SDK 声明；当大模型判定需要使用对应工具时，可自主调用 `tool_activate({ namespace })` 按需挂载。内置 LRU 策略（上限 3 个活跃命名空间），自动淘汰最久未用的命名空间，激活状态在会话压缩与恢复后完整重建，兼具海量工具接入能力与极致小巧的静态 Schema 面。\n- **关键事实登记簿与就近状态投射（Fact Register & Working Context）**：长程多轮对话中大模型极易遗忘早期的关键业务约束或踩过的坑。插件向模型提供专属 `fact_register` 工具，可将用户硬性约束、已确认的架构决策或失败路径登记为单行事实（每条不超过 160 字符，最多保留 12 条）。关键事实随 `[Working Context: ...]` 状态行在每一轮交互中就近投射至最新消息尾部的局部注意力窗口内，从物理机制上彻底解决长上下文“中间遗忘”与重复踩坑顽疾。\n- **原生调度者架构与敏捷访谈纪律（Dispatcher Identity & Triage）**：预设出厂深度集成调度者（Dispatcher）架构规范，赋能模型以团队指挥官身份统领工程任务。内置复杂度分诊机制（L0/L1 单点任务直接敏捷执行，L2 复杂任务严格遵循“澄清访谈 -> 架构规划 -> 并发子代理派发 -> 双层严格验收”标准流）；设定严格的提问预算控制（单轮最多 4 问、总计最多 3 轮、影响面排序、假设先行），杜绝无效拉扯；任务状态权威沉淀于 `todo_write`，杜绝浮躁的敷衍式交付。\n- **新建会话老虎机拨杆与炫酷中奖特效（Composer Slot Lever）**：在新建会话输入框工具行、模型选择器左侧，精心打造了一台复古老虎机拨杆控件。下拉拨杆（支持鼠标拖拽、单击或键盘快捷操作）即可一键为当前新建会话装配梁神模式，拉下命中即触发绚丽的中奖粒子特效（闪光、冲击环、火花粒子与专属彩蛋横幅）；上推即可平滑切回默认模式。拨杆自适应全局主题色彩，且在会话开始后自动隐藏，丝滑灵动，极具极客趣味。\n\n详细机制、评测数据与高级配置参数见 [dsh-liangshen README](packages/dsh-liangshen/README.zh.md)。\n\n### 移动端远程控制（Mobile Remote · 手机访问与跨设备触控优化）\n\n通过侧边栏底部的手机图标打开设备配对面板。使用手机扫码或复制链接配对后，手机浏览器将直接载入官方 Web GUI，并自动激活移动端触控交互层：轻触鲸鱼图标唤出侧边栏、支持手势左滑收起与右滑展开、长按会话项目呼出操作菜单、软键盘 Enter 键仅用于换行、输入框采用 16px 字体防止页面聚焦缩放。适合桌面屏幕的扩展面板（如 SSH 终端、任务看板、Git 图谱等）在手机端自动隐藏，聚焦于会话管理、模型切换、思考强度调整与消息收发，多端实时共享完整上下文状态。\n\n同一配对通道同样支持另一台 PC 浏览器接入：在远程电脑访问配对链接即可运行完整的桌面版 Web GUI。所有远程通信均受配对门控保护（走 `/remote/api` 路径），未经验证的访问将被拦截并仅显示提示横幅。配对令牌具备单次使用与超时失效机制，点击“停止”可立即吊销所有已连接设备。二维码默认基于局域网通信，搭配 cloudflared 等隧道工具可实现安全的公网跨网络访问。为确保安全性，使用隧道时建议走配对通道，不建议为隧道域名配置 `--trusted-host` 参数，避免绕过设备验证门控（详见[远程控制插件说明](packages/dsh-remote-web-ui/README.zh.md)）。\n\n![DeepSeek Harness 手机端与桌面端 Web ![DeepSeek 手机端模型切换弹层 — 多供应商与思考档位快速选择](docs/screenshots/23-mobile-model-sheet.png) |\n\n### 远程连接（SSH Ops · Web 终端、SFTP 传输与集群运维）\n\n通过侧边栏“SSH”入口打开远程运维面板。支持密钥与密码认证，可一键导入本地 `~/.ssh/config` 主机列表；配置数据安全保存在 安全地址；\n- **集群并发执行**：支持多主机批量命令执行，并可通过别名、运行环境或标签进行过滤；\n- **Agent 直连调用**：智能体与面板共享主机配置，在会话中发出指令即可委派 Agent 执行远程巡检与运维命令。\n\n### 使用统计（Usage Statistics · Token 消耗追踪、余额预警与 Token 银行）\n\n在“设置 > 使用统计”中集中查看 token 消耗数据、供应商余额以及编程套餐额度，支持自动定时刷新与手动即时查询。\n\n- **用量明细**：查看每日输入、输出与缓存用量，按不同供应商与模型细分展示，并提供最近 30 天消费趋势；支持的供应商提供账户余额查询，针对 DeepSeek 官方路由还提供峰谷分时计费与账单估算。\n- **个人套餐追踪**：实时展示 Kimi、GLM、MiniMax、OpenCode Go、Codex / ChatGPT 等平台编程套餐的使用比例与重置周期。\n- **Token 银行**：所有 provider 每消耗 100 万 tokens 铸造 1 鲸元，以“鲸元券”形式展示台账周期内的累计 token 与调用指标，支持保存票券卡片与系统级分享。\n- **桌面宠物联动**：安装宠物插件后，可通过桌面悬浮挂件的气泡提示直接查看当前会话供应商的额度、余额或今日消耗。\n\n统计自插件首次启用起计，不回填历史数据；鲸元券统计台账窗口内所有 provider 的 tokens（消费行仍只来自 DeepSeek 官方余额观测）。支持的供应商列表与配置细节见 [dsh-usage README](packages/dsh-usage/README.zh.md)。\n\n![DeepSeek Token 用量统计与 Token 银行 — API 消耗追踪与账单估算](docs/screenshots/35-usage-token-bank.webp)\n\n### Git 图谱（Git Graph · 分支可视化与 Worktree 会话隔离）\n\n在对话输入框上方集成 |\n\n### 会话归档管理（Session Archive Manager · 全文检索与生命周期策略）\n\n会话归档管理（`dsh-session-archive`）是专为解决大量长短期会话堆积而设计的集中管理模块，随全家桶安装生效：\n\n- **集中检索与状态筛选**：统一呈现活跃会话、已归档会话、空白会话、子代理派生会话以及无工作区会话，支持按标题、工作区、状态及会话 ID 进行关键词搜索与多维排序；\n- **安全批量操作**：支持跨筛选结果的多选批量归档、批量恢复以及级联物理删除。执行物理删除时系统将明确提示受影响的后代会话数与预计释放空间，大批量删除需二次确认；当前处于运行中或带有运行中子代理的会话受到严格保护，防止误删；\n- **自动化生命周期策略**：提供两个默认关闭的自动化策略：根据最后活跃时间自动归档、根据归档时间自动清理超期数据，支持在启用前进行结果预览与单次手动执行。\n\n删除操作不可逆，所有管理路由严格限制本机回环访问。详细机制见 [dsh-session-archive README](packages/dsh-session-archive/README.zh.md)。\n\n### 暗黑沉浸风格预览](docs/screenshots/17-skin-blue-fantasy-dark.png)\n\n## 快速上手\n\n### 系统要求\n\n- 已安装 DeepSeek Harness 且 `dsh web` 可正常启动。\n- npm 安装方式无需额外环境；若从源码仓库构建，需要 Node.js >= 22 与 pnpm 环境。\n\n### 三步上手（npm 安装，推荐）\n\n- **DSH Web CLI（现有浏览器服务）**：\n  1. 先完成三项构建脚本审批（见“安装排障”），再安装聚合包：`dsh plugin --profile web add @linxin666/dsh-web-all@latest`\n  2. 重启 `dsh web` 服务，侧边栏将自动呈现各插件入口\n  3. 打开“设置 > `@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-skin-center`。若因包管理器门禁安装到旧版本，请参阅后文“安装排障”。\n\n### 从 GitHub 仓库直接安装\n\n仓库根目录声明了标准 `dsh.bundle` 装配清单，支持直接通过仓库地址安装，无需手动克隆代码与构建：\n\n```sh\ndsh plugin --profile web add [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md)。\n\n### 安装排障\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>展开查看常见安装与构建排障方案</strong></summary>\n\n<br>\n\n> **pnpm 严格依赖隔离导致模块找不到**：pnpm 的 isolated 模式默认仅将聚合包放置在顶层，部分子包可能被嵌套收敛，导致 `dsh web` 启动时报错 `Cannot find package '@linxin666/dsh-...'`。若遇到此情况，可在 profile 目录的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 中添加配置 `nodeLinker: hoisted`（或 `public-hoist-pattern: ['@linxin666/*']`）后重新安装。\n\n> **构建脚本被拦截 (ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS)**：这三项审批必须在首次 add 之前就位。正确顺序是重置 profile（官方 `--from-default-profile web`）或换新 profile，把 `cloudflared`、`cpu-features`、`ssh2` 写进 `<profile>/pnpm-workspace.yaml` 的 `allowBuilds`，再执行 add。装失败后补审批重跑会 exit 0，但 `dsh.profile.bundles` 仍无该行：静默半挂载，重跑修不回来。已带审批的存量 profile 升级不受影响。\n\n> **pnpm 11 发布时间门禁问题**：在包版本发布后的短时间内，pnpm 11 的默认安全策略（`minimumReleaseAge`）可能会尝试回退拉取旧版本。建议在 profile 目录的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 中排除相关命名空间以确保获取最新版本：\n>\n> ```yaml\n> minimumReleaseAgeExclude:\n>   - '@linxin666/*'\n> ```\n\n</details>\n\n## 兼容性与运行环境\n\ndsh-web 针对主流操作系统、现代化浏览器及网络拓扑进行了深度工程调优与兼容性保障：\n\n| 维度 | 支持范围与技术规格 |\n| --- | --- |\n| 宿主运行环境 | DeepSeek Harness CLI (`dsh web`)、官方桌面客户端（DeepSeek Harness Desktop） |\n| 操作系统 | macOS (Apple Silicon M 系列 & Intel 芯片)、Windows 10/11 (含 WSL2)、Linux (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch, CentOS 等) |\n| 浏览器与设备 | 桌面浏览器 (Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox)；移动端现代浏览器 (iOS Safari, Android Chrome 等) |\n| 网络连接架构 | 本机环回访问 (127.0.0.1)、局域网多设备互联 (LAN)、公网隧道安全穿透 (Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale, FRP, Nginx 反向代理) |\n| 模型供应商覆盖 | DeepSeek 官方通道与满血模型、OpenAI (GPT-4o 等)、Anthropic Claude、Google Gemini、Kimi (Moonshot)、GLM (智谱)、MiniMax、Ollama 本地大模型、SiliconFlow 等 |\n| 运行时依赖 | npm 方式安装无特殊环境依赖；源码编译需 Node.js >= 22 与 pnpm >= 9 |\n\n## 常见问题\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>安装重启后，侧边栏未显示插件入口？</strong></summary>\n\n请首先检查插件是否正确安装至 `web` profile（命令需包含 `--profile web`），并通过 `dsh --profile web --dump-config` 验证配置层是否已成功挂载。注意仅刷新网页无法加载新模块，必须彻底重启 `dsh web` 后端服务进程。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>定时任务为何未能按时触发执行？</strong></summary>\n\n任务调度完全由 `dsh web` 后端宿主进程驱动，无需保持前端浏览器页面打开。若宿主进程退出、系统关机或整机进入深度睡眠，错过的触发时间点将遵循跳过策略处理，不执行回填补跑；若任务到达触发点时上一轮仍在运行，会自动顺延至下一个周期。若需要允许息屏但防止主机自动睡眠，可开启任务看板自带的电源保护选项。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>手机端配对后为何没有收到流式推送？</strong></summary>\n\n流式推送走官方 WebSocket 通道，配对后经门控的 `/remote` 代理转发。隧道中断期间更新暂停，通道恢复后继续，无需重新配对；更新节奏的差异来自远程链路的广域网往返延迟。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>试穿主题皮肤不满意如何还原？</strong></summary>\n\n皮肤面板提供免落盘试穿功能：点击试穿即刻在当前界面生效预览，离开面板或关闭预览会自动恢复初始外观；只有显式点击“应用”按钮才会将主题配置写入磁盘，可放心预览各类主题。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>是否可以仅使用主题皮肤或某个单一插件？</strong></summary>\n\n完全支持。若仅需要视觉定制，直接安装 `@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-skin-center` 即可；若仅需特定功能，参考“单独安装某个插件”章节直接安装对应 npm 包即可。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>已安装全家桶的前提下，能否额外独立安装某个子插件？</strong></summary>\n\n可以。聚合包内部的插件注册标识均统一带有 `web-ui-` 前缀（例如 `web-ui-usage`），与独立包的原生标识（如 `usage`）相互独立，不会产生 loader entry 重复冲突。宿主服务对同类插件会自动去重。通常情况下安装全家桶即可满足完整需求，无需重复安装单个子包。\n\n</details>\n\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>如何通过手机或平板远程访问 DeepSeek Harness？是否必须在同一 Wi-Fi 下？</strong></summary>\n\n手机远程访问基于配对令牌安全门控。若手机与运行 DSH 的电脑处于同一局域网（Wi-Fi），电脑端点击侧边栏手机图标弹出二维码，手机直接扫码即可打开完整的移动端交互界面。若需要公网跨网络访问（例如在户外使用移动蜂窝网络访问家中电脑），可搭配 Cloudflare Tunnel（例如 cloudflared）或 Tailscale 将 DSH 端口穿透至公网，手机打开公网链接配对访问即可，通信全程走鉴权通道，未配对请求将被严格拦截。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>关闭浏览器或电脑休眠后，DeepSeek 的定时任务还会继续运行吗？</strong></summary>\n\n任务调度完全由 `dsh web` 后端宿主进程驱动，关闭浏览器标签页不影响定时任务的触发与执行。但如果整机进入深度睡眠或关机，宿主进程将暂停运行，离线期间错过的触发点会遵循跳过策略处理。若希望保持无人值守后台自动化，可在任务看板设置中开启“电源保护”选项，该选项会阻止系统因空闲进入休眠（允许显示器正常熄灭），确保定时任务准时触发。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>如何查看和监控 DeepSeek 及其他模型 API 的 Token 消耗与账户余额？</strong></summary>\n\n安装使用统计插件后，在“设置 > 使用统计”面板中可查看按日汇总的输入、输出与缓存 Token 数量，支持按模型细分查看 30 天消费趋势。针对 DeepSeek 官方路由还提供峰谷分时计费估算；若配置了支持查询余额的供应商 API，插件可定时拉取当前账户剩余额度与重置周期。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>多个 AI 智能体（Agent）并发编码时，如何避免 Git 分支和代码冲突？</strong></summary>\n\n直接在单一 Git 工作区并发运行多个智能体容易导致代码互相覆盖。使用全家桶内置的 Git 图谱插件，可以在新建会话时自动或手动创建独立的 Git Worktree。每个智能体会话在各自专属的分支和物理目录中独立运行、提交修改，彻底隔绝主工作区文件，开发完成后可在图谱面板中清晰比对并合并分支。\n\n</details>\n\n## 已知限制\n\n- 任务看板由后端 Host 进程统一调度，关闭前端标签页不影响任务执行；但若宿主进程停止或操作系统关机睡眠，处于离线期间的触发点将直接跳过不补跑。可选的电源保护仅阻止系统闲置睡眠，无法阻止用户主动合盖、手动休眠或电源切断，技术细节见 [dsh-task-board README](packages/dsh-task-board/README.zh.md)。\n- SSH 凭据（密码与私钥口令）保存在本地 `~/.dsh/dsh-ssh.json` 文件中（文件权限为 0600）；在网络中断重连时可能重新发送非幂等命令，终端输出保持原样返回不执行脱敏，安全规范见 [dsh-ssh README](packages/dsh-ssh/README.zh.md)。\n- 移动端流式输出经隧道或固定域名中继转发，广域网往返延迟叠加在每次更新上；固定域名中继比裸快速隧道多一跳，两者都可用。\n- 从源码构建全仓需要 Node.js >= 22 与 pnpm 工具链，直接从 npm 安装不受此限制。\n\n## 社区\n\n欢迎加入社区交流群，与开发者及其他用户探讨使用技巧、反馈使用问题或提出新功能建议。\n\n扫描下方二维码加入“DSH Web 交流群”：\n\n<img src=\"docs/community-center.jpg\" alt=\"DeepSeek Harness '@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer/client'\nimport type { ConnectionHandle } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection/client'\nimport { FooterRemoteEntry } from './FooterRemoteEntry.tsx'\nimport { './settings-entry-form.ts'\n\n// Portrait-touch adaptation of the official UI: installed under the plugin\n// lifecycle (apply) so disabling the plugin in cordis patch (disabled: true)\n// leaves the './PairFailedNotice.tsx'\nexport type { RemoteKey } from './locales.ts'\nexport type { RemoteSettingsCardFace, RemoteSettingsCardState } from './RemoteSettingsCard.tsx'\n\ndeclare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-slots' {\n  interface LocaleNamespaceMap {\n    /** Mobile remote-control surface copy. */\n    remote: RemoteKey\n  }\n\n  interface SlotMap {\n    /**\n     * The sidebar foot seat beside the settings trigger, declared by the\n     * sidebar shell on deployments that carry the feature seat; the shell\n     * passes only its column display state.\n     */\n    /**\n     * The child slot the Web UI plugin group declares; this card registers\n     * into the group's list seat rather than the official\n     * bundle-configuration seat. Spelled here with the same shape so this\n     * package can register without depending on the sibling UI package.\n     */\n    'web-ui.plugin.item': { kind: 'list'; scope: 'root'; owner: SettingsPluginItemOwnerProps }\n  }\n}\n\n/** Owner share of the sidebar remote-control seat: the column display state the trigger renders against. */\nexport interface SidebarRemoteOwnerProps {\n  /** Whether the sidebar renders wide content (false = 56px rail). */\n  wide: boolean\n}\n\n/** Owner share of a plugin card (the section supplies nothing). */\nexport interface SettingsPluginItemOwnerProps {\n  /** Marker field: card owner props are intentionally empty. */\n  children?: never\n}\n\ndeclare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {\n  interface Context {\n    /**\n     * Optional family settings binder provided by dsh-web-settings; absent\n     * when that group plugin is not installed, so callers fall back to the\n     * official `ctx.configForms` service.\n     *\n     * The 0.1.7 client addresses one form per active profile entry id and\n     * carries no package identity, so the family binder resolves a family\n     * settings namespace to the entry that owns it and hands back that entry's\n     * shared form; the official service is addressed by the entry id directly.\n     */\n    webUiSettings?: {\n      bind<S>(spec: { namespace: string; decode?: (section: unknown) => S | undefined }): ConfigForm<S>\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n\n/** Dictionary namespace owned by this plugin. */\nconst NS = 'remote'\n\n/**\n * Settings namespace the remote-control card edits: the family identity of\n * this plugin's own settings form, and the row id a standalone bundle install\n * carries.\n */\nconst REMOTE_WEB_UI_NS = 'remote-web-ui'\n\n/** Profile entry id the family aggregate's generated row carries. */\nconst AGGREGATE_ENTRY_ID = 'web-ui-remote-web-ui'\n\n/** Profile entry ids this package's patch rows carry, most specific first. */\nconst REMOTE_WEB_UI_ENTRY_IDS: readonly string[] = [AGGREGATE_ENTRY_ID, 'ui-remote-web-ui', REMOTE_WEB_UI_NS]\n\n/**\n * The profile entry id this package's own row carries, for a page that serves\n * no family binder.\n *\n * The shared describe mirror answers asynchronously, so at plugin activation it\n * usually holds nothing yet — and an unanswered or empty mirror is not evidence\n * of absence. Binding the bare namespace there left the card bound to an entry\n * the Host does not serve, and the form is bound once per session, so the card\n * never recovered (every save answered `No configurable plugin entry`). The\n * aggregate row id matches nearly every deployment; only a mirror that answers\n * with OTHER plugins' rows falls back to the namespace itself (the pre-0.1.7\n * keying shape), because that answer is the one that actually proves this\n * package's own row is not served.\n * @param forms - the shared configuration forms service.\n * @returns the entry id to bind.\n */\nexport function servedEntryId(forms: ConfigForms): string {\n  let served: readonly string[] | undefined\n  try {\n    served = forms.describe().getSnapshot().view?.namespaces.map(view => view.ns)\n  } catch {\n    // A mirror that refuses the read is unanswered too, not absent.\n    served = undefined\n  }\n  if (served === undefined || served.length === 0) return AGGREGATE_ENTRY_ID\n  return REMOTE_WEB_UI_ENTRY_IDS.find(id => served.includes(id)) ?? REMOTE_WEB_UI_NS\n}\n\n/**\n * Bind the settings form the remote-control card reads and writes.\n *\n * The family binder comes first: it resolves this package's family namespace\n * onto the profile entry id the Host serves the form under, and keeps the\n * loopback bridge as its own fallback. A page without that group (or one where\n * its client half has not applied yet) binds through the shared forms service,\n * on the entry id the describe mirror justifies and rebound as soon as the\n * mirror answers — see {@link createServedEntryForm}.\n * @param ctx - client context carrying the family binder and/or the shared forms service.\n * @returns the form the card stages and saves through.\n */\nexport function bindSettingsForm(ctx: ClientContext): ConfigForm<RemoteSettings> {\n  const family = ctx.get('webUiSettings')\n  if (family !== undefined && typeof family.bind === 'function') {\n    return family.bind<RemoteSettings>({ namespace: REMOTE_WEB_UI_NS })\n  }\n  return createServedEntryForm<RemoteSettings>({\n    forms: ctx.configForms,\n    entryIds: REMOTE_WEB_UI_ENTRY_IDS,\n  })\n}\n\n/** Heartbeat cadence from a paired phone (presence + revocation liveness). */\nconst HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 10_000\n\n/** Services required by this plugin. injects mobile CSS, gesture hooks, or the whale floating button.\n  startMobileAdapt()\n  ctx.effect(() => () => {\n    ;(window as unknown as { __dshRemoteAdapt?: RemoteAdaptGlobal }).__dshRemoteAdapt?.setEnabled?.(false)\n  }, 'remote-web-ui: mobile-adapt')\n\n  // Anonymous install heartbeat (docs/telemetry.md): one beat per browser per\n  // UTC day, package name only, silent failure.\n  reportDailyHeartbeat([{ name: '@linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui' }])\n\n  ctx.effect(() => {\n    try {\n      return ctx.locale.register(NS, { zh, en })\n    } catch {\n      return () => {}\n    }\n  }, 'remote-web-ui: dictionaries')\n\n  // The mobile adapt's whale button expands the collapsed sidebar and the\n  // activation closes the details panel — both through the official layout\n  // service (ctx.layout.toggleSidebar / closeDetails flip the panel state;\n  // the narrow-viewport semantics open the drawer).\n  const layout = ctx.get('layout') as { toggleSidebar?: () => void; closeDetails?: () => void } | undefined\n  const adapt = (window as unknown as { __dshRemoteAdapt?: RemoteAdaptGlobal }).__dshRemoteAdapt\n  // The official layout face throws (by contract) when the root entry has\n  // not mounted yet; these closures also fire from gestures racing that\n  // first mount, so they tolerate the throw instead of surfacing it.\n  const layoutCall = (call: (() => void) | undefined): void => {\n    try {\n      call?.()\n    } catch {\n      // Boot-order throw: the panel action is a no-op before the root entry.\n    }\n  }\n  if (layout !== undefined && adapt !== undefined) {\n    if (typeof layout.toggleSidebar === 'function') {\n      adapt.toggleSidebar = () => {\n        layoutCall(layout.toggleSidebar)\n      }\n    }\n    if (typeof layout.closeDetails === 'function') {\n      adapt.closeDetails = () => {\n        layoutCall(layout.closeDetails)\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  if (adapt !== undefined && adapt.toggleSidebar === null) {\n (document.querySelector('[class$=\"_railFish\"] button, [class$=\"_logoRow\"] [class*=\"_iconButton\"]') as HTMLElement | null)?.click()\n    }\n  }\n\n  const t = ctx.locale.bind(NS)\n  // Hand the `remote` translate seat to the module-scope adaptation layer:\n  // the whale label was rendered with the English fallback before any\n  // dictionary existed; the wiring plus the layer's own sync Sends are fire-and-forget:\n * failures stay silent and simply retry on a later mount or day. Frames where\n * storage is unavailable report nothing.\n *\n * The family-wide opt-out and the browser's Do Not Track signal both suppress\n * the heartbeat; the Web Plugins settings switch writes the same localStorage\n * key. The system is documented in docs/telemetry.md.\n */\n\nexport type TelemetryChannel = 'market' | 'npm' | 'unknown'\n\nexport interface TelemetryItem {\n  /** npm package name or asset id, e.g. \"@linxin666/dsh-pet\" or \"skin:harbor\". */\n  name: string\n  /** Installed version when known; omitted otherwise. */\n  version?: string\n  /** Install channel when determinable (market = Workshop install). */\n  channel?: TelemetryChannel\n}\n\n/** localStorage key carrying the family-wide telemetry opt-out ('1' = off). */\nexport const TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT_KEY = 'dsh-web-ui-telemetry-opt-out'\n\nconst VISITOR_KEY = 'dsh-web-ui-telemetry-visitor'\nconst DAY_KEY_PREFIX = 'dsh-web-ui-telemetry-day:'\nconst ENDPOINT = 'https://dsh-market.com/api/telemetry/event'\n\n// Baked into each client bundle by shared/tsdown.client.ts (the package's own\n// package.json version at build time). Undefined in dev/test builds.\ndeclare const __DSH_PKG_VERSION__: string | undefined\n\n/** The building package's version, when the bundle carries it. */\nfunction bakedVersion(): string | undefined {\n  try {\n    return typeof __DSH_PKG_VERSION__ === 'string' && __DSH_PKG_VERSION__ !== ''\n      ? __DSH_PKG_VERSION__\n      : undefined\n  } catch {\n    return undefined\n  }\n}\n\n/** Whether the user switched the family-wide opt-out on (reads storage only). */\nexport function isTelemetryOptedOut(): boolean {\n  try {\n    return localStorage.getItem(TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT_KEY) === '1'\n  } catch {\n    // Storage unavailable: there is no stored opt-out to honour.\n    return false\n  }\n}\n\n/** Turn the family-wide opt-out on or off (writing '1' / removing the key); never throws. */\nexport function setTelemetryOptedOut(optedOut: boolean): void {\n  try {\n    if (optedOut) localStorage.setItem(TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT_KEY, '1')\n    else localStorage.removeItem(TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT_KEY)\n  } catch {\n    // Storage unavailable: the preference cannot be persisted on this machine.\n  }\n}\n\n/** Whether the browser itself asks not to be tracked; a failed read means no signal. */\nfunction doNotTrackRequested(): boolean {\n  try {\n    // '1' per the DNT header spec, 'yes' from older Firefox builds.\n    return navigator.doNotTrack === '1' || navigator.doNotTrack === 'yes'\n  } catch {\n    return false\n  }\n}\n\n/** Whether a heartbeat must be suppressed right now: opt-out stored, or the browser asks not to be tracked. */\nexport function isTelemetrySuppressed(): boolean {\n  return isTelemetryOptedOut() || doNotTrackRequested()\n}\n\n/** Read or lazily create the anonymous visitor id; null when storage is unavailable. */\nfunction visitorId(): string | null {\n  try {\n    const existing = localStorage.getItem(VISITOR_KEY)\n    if (existing && /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$/.test(existing)) return existing\n    const fresh = crypto.randomUUID().replaceAll('-', '')\n    localStorage.setItem(VISITOR_KEY, fresh)\n    return fresh\n  } catch {\n    // Storage unavailable (privacy mode, sandboxed frame): report nothing.\n    return null\n  }\n}\n\n/** Drop stale per-day dedup keys so localStorage does not grow forever. */\nfunction pruneDayKeys(today: string): void {\n  try {\n    for (let index = localStorage.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {\n      const key = localStorage.key(index)\n      if (key !== null && key.startsWith(DAY_KEY_PREFIX) && key !== DAY_KEY_PREFIX + today) {\n        localStorage.removeItem(key)\n      }\n    }\n  } catch { /* best effort */ }\n}\n\n/**\n * Fire the daily heartbeat for the given items at most once per UTC day per\n * browser. Never throws and never blocks the caller. Items without an explicit\n * version inherit the bundle's baked build version.\n */\nexport function reportDailyHeartbeat(items: readonly TelemetryItem[]): void {\n  try {\n    // First guard: a stored opt-out or the browser's Do Not Track stops every\n    // read below from minting an id, marking the day, or reaching the network.\n    if (isTelemetrySuppressed()) return\n    if (items.length === 0) return\n    const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)\n    // Automation contexts (CDP-driven QA browsers, fresh isolated profiles)\n    // mint a new visitor id per run and would inflate instance counts.\n    if (navigator.webdriver) return\n    if (localStorage.getItem(DAY_KEY_PREFIX + today) !== null) return\n    const visitor = visitorId()\n    if (visitor === null) return\n    pruneDayKeys(today)\n    const payloadItems = items.map((item) => {\n      const out: Record<string, string> = { name: item.name }\n      const version = item.version ?? bakedVersion()\n      if (version !== undefined) out.version = version\n      if (item.channel !== undefined) out.channel = item.channel\n      return out\n    })\n    const body = JSON.stringify({ kind: 'heartbeat', visitor, items: payloadItems })\n    void fetch(ENDPOINT, {\n      method: 'POST',\n      headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },\n      body,\n      keepalive: true,\n    }).then((response) => {\n      // Mark the day only after an accepted send, so offline browsers retry\n      // on a later mount instead of going dark until tomorrow.\n      if (response.ok) localStorage.setItem(DAY_KEY_PREFIX + today, '1')\n    }).catch(() => { /* unreachable endpoint: stay silent */ })\n  } catch { /* never break the host UI over telemetry */ }\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * The `api/gate` listener: application-level access control layered on top\n * of the transport fence (the fence is Host/Origin based and explicitly not\n * an authentication layer — packages/client/connection documents this\n * event as the sanctioned seam for pairing/revocation).\n *\n * Policy: loopback requests (the desktop) pass without a device identity;\n * every non-loopback /api request must carry a live, non-revoked device\n * cookie — intended to make the QR the only way into a LAN-exposed dsh web\n * and to give \"停止\" real teeth for direct /api callers.\n *\n * Cohort reality (0.1.2-alpha.2): NOTHING emits api/gate in the official\n * runtime, so this listener never fires there and direct /api is governed\n * solely by the harness fence + browser-auth cookie. The pairing gate with\n * real teeth lives on the plugin's own /remote channel (remote-api.ts); the\n * listener stays wired for cohort lines that do carry the seam, and the\n * README security model states the gap plainly.\n */\n\nimport type { IncomingMessage } from 'node:http'\nimport type { PairingService } from './pairing.ts'\nimport { isLoopbackAddress, isLoopbackHostname, isProxiedRequest } from './loopback.ts'\n\n/**\n * Read one cookie value from a Cookie header.\n * @param header - the raw Cookie header value (or undefined).\n * @param name - the cookie name.\n * @returns the value, or undefined when absent.\n */\nexport function readCookie(header: string | undefined, name: string): string | undefined {\n  if (header === undefined) return undefined\n  for (const part of header.split(';')) {\n    const eq = part.indexOf('=')\n    if (eq < 0) continue\n    const key = part.slice(0, eq).trim()\n    if (key === name) return part.slice(eq + 1).trim()\n  }\n  return undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * The effective Host hostname of a request.\n * @param request - node HTTP request.\n * @returns the normalized hostname, or undefined when unparsable.\n */\nexport function hostnameOf(request: IncomingMessage): string | undefined {\n  const host = request.headers.host\n  if (typeof host !== 'string') return undefined\n  try {\n    return new URL(`http://${host}`).hostname\n  } catch {\n    return undefined\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether the request arrived at this process over a loopback upstream: a\n * loopback socket and a loopback Host header, with the forwarding headers\n * deliberately ignored. A reverse proxy (a Cloudflare tunnel, frp, nginx) dials\n * 127.0.0.1:<port> and rewrites the Host to that upstream literal, so this is\n * the shape of a tunneled request as much as of the desktop one.\n *\n * It answers \"this process is reachable at a loopback authority\", never \"this\n * request is the desktop\": the desktop decision is {@link isLoopbackClient},\n * which a forwarded request never satisfies. Only the fences that decide whether\n * a Host is answerable at all (the pairing status view, the reachability beacon,\n * the pairing entry pages) may be built on this predicate; every decision that\n * hands out a credential or the desktop payload stays on {@link isLoopbackClient}\n * (issue #1919 keeps #1906 shut: reachability for the visitor, payload and\n * control plane for the desktop).\n * @param request - node HTTP request.\n * @returns true when the socket and the Host both name loopback.\n */\nexport function isLoopbackUpstream(request: IncomingMessage): boolean {\n  const hostname = hostnameOf(request)\n  if (hostname === undefined || !isLoopbackHostname(hostname)) return false\n  const socket = request.socket as { remoteAddress?: string } | undefined\n  return isLoopbackAddress(socket?.remoteAddress)\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether a request comes from the desktop loopback client: a loopback upstream\n * ({@link isLoopbackUpstream}) reached with no forwarding header. This is the\n * same decision the shared copy makes in `isLoopbackRequest` (sans the browser\n * same-origin markers, which the /api/pair routes apply separately through\n * `isTrustedApiRequest`), and it carries the same proxy rule: a reverse proxy\n * rewrites the Host to its own 127.0.0.1:<port> upstream and connects over\n * loopback, so a request that arrives with CF-Connecting-IP or X-Forwarded-For\n * is a forwarded one and is never the desktop (issue #1906). Every decision\n * that grants the desktop payload or a control plane (the api/gate listener,\n * the events stream, /api/pair/issue, /api/pair/stop, /api/pair/revoke,\n * /api/pair/lan-bind) reads this predicate, so the rule holds for all of them.\n * @param request - node HTTP request.\n * @returns true for a local desktop request with no proxy in front of it.\n */\nexport function isLoopbackClient(request: IncomingMessage): boolean {\n  if (isProxiedRequest(request)) return false\n  return isLoopbackUpstream(request)\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the api/gate listener for one pairing service.\n * @param service - the pairing service.\n * @param requirePairingForLan - when false, non-loopback requests pass\n * without a device cookie (the feature then only manages tokens/status;\n * revocation of paired devices still holds). A function is re-read per\n * request, so a settings edit takes effect without a restart. Defaults to true.\n * @param enabled - when false, every non-loopback request is vetoed while\n * loopback stays available. A function is re-read per request so the fence\n * stays mounted for the plugin lifetime and disabling the plugin cannot open\n * a LAN-exposed /api. Defaults to true.\n * @returns the cordis waterfall listener: call `next()` to delegate,\n * return false (without calling it) to veto with 403.\n */\nexport function makeGateListener(\n  service: PairingService,\n  requirePairingForLan: boolean | (() => boolean) = true,\n  enabled: boolean | (() => boolean) = true,\n): (request: IncomingMessage, method: string | undefined, next: () => boolean | Promise<boolean>) => boolean | Promise<boolean> {\n  return (request, _method, next) => {\n    // Loopback clients (desktop at 127.0.0.1) always pass without cookie check.\n    if (isLoopbackClient(request)) return next()\n    const active = typeof enabled === 'function' ? enabled() : enabled\n    if (!active) return false\n    const require = typeof requirePairingForLan === 'function' ? requirePairingForLan() : requirePairingForLan\n    // When pairing is not required for LAN, non-loopback requests pass too.\n    if (!require) return next()\n    // Non-loopback origin: verify paired-device cookie. Sibling plugins that\n    // own their own prefixes (/pet, /git, /sidebar, …) consult the same cookie\n    // through the remoteWebUiPairing service — this listener only covers /api.\n    return isPairedDeviceRequest(service, request) ? next() : false\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether a request carries a live, non-revoked paired-device cookie for\n * this service. Sibling host routes outside /api (the right-panel\n * /sidebar/* routes, etc.) use the same check via the remoteWebUiPairing service.\n * @param service - the pairing service that owns the device table.\n * @param request - the incoming HTTP request.\n * @returns true when the cookie names a live session (and lastSeenAt was refreshed).\n */\nexport function isPairedDeviceRequest(service: PairingService, request: IncomingMessage): boolean {\n  const deviceId = readCookie(request.headers.cookie, service.config.cookieName)\n  if (deviceId === undefined) return false\n  return service.touchDevice(deviceId)\n}\n"

from './detached-work.ts'\nimport { REMOTE_CHANNEL_BOOT_SCRIPT } from './remote-channel-boot.ts'\nimport { UUID_POLYFILL_SCRIPT } from './uuid-polyfill.ts'\n\ndeclare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {\n  interface Events {\n    /**\n     * Volatile config values were committed into the running fiber without a\n     * remount; dispatched to the owning fiber only. Stored as a settings secret and read back redacted;\n   * sent only to `https://api.cloudflare.com` and never to a log line, a status\n   * frame, a child process argument, or a browser-visible field.\n   */\n  cfApiToken?: string\n  /** Cloudflare account id the named tunnel belongs to (`cfAccountId`). */\n  cfAccountId?: string\n  /** The named tunnel's id — not its run token (`cfTunnelId`). */\n  cfTunnelId?: string\n  /**\n   * Stable-origin relay: when on (default), the quick tunnel is fronted by a\n   * fixed `https://<id>.dsh-market.com` subdomain (the dsh-market worker's\n   * registry), so the phone's bookmark and pairing cookie survive `dsh web`\n   * restarts without any user setup. The marker\n * is also what admits a write and what keeps the edit on the live path — the\n * Loader commits the new value into the field's reference and announces\n * `loader/volatile-update` on this fiber instead of remounting the row, so the\n * pairing service, its device sessions, the tunnel and the route registrations\n * survive a settings save (see {@link applyImpl}'s sync).\n *\n * The A recompose\n    // pass can run this apply before the listener binds: defer the tunnel\n    // branch (and re-plan on a short timer) instead of minting an\n    // http://127.0.0.1:undefined target; everything else in sync applies.\n    // Read through the normalizer: a half-read webServer can hand NaN/Infinity,\n    // and that must take the unbound-port path (settle retry, no request) rather\n    // than mint a \":NaN\" target or leave every dependent surface waiting.\n    const livePort = livePortOf(ctx.webServer.port)\n    const tunnelNeedsPort = livePort === undefined && value.autoTunnel === true\n    if (tunnelNeedsPort) {\n      if (!portSettleWarned) {\n        portSettleWarned = true\n        console.warn('remote-web-ui: autoTunnel is on but the web server port is not bound yet — the quick tunnel starts once the port settles')\n      }\n      schedulePortSettleRetry()\n    } else {\n      portSettleWarned = false\n      applyTunnelPlan(value, livePort)\n    }\n    // The ingress sync learns the live port in both branches: an unbound\n    // listener is a zero-request wait there, and the same settle timer delivers\n    // the port — no second retry loop of its own.\n    scheduleIngressSync(value, livePort)\n    if (livePort === undefined && !tunnelNeedsPort && value.ingressSync === true) schedulePortSettleRetry()\n    // The lease and the bridge are transport-owned, not tunnel-owned: a\n    // bridge-mode instance has to reach its object even when no quick tunnel\n    // runs (the claim is the only answer that carries the bridge grant, and\n    // without it the edge reports no-connector forever). The dedupe key keeps\n    // a settings sync from re-claiming, and a fresh quick URL re-claims.\n    if (value.enabled && value.relay !== false) {\n      if (livePort === undefined) schedulePortSettleRetry()\n      else claimRelayLeaseFor(livePort, publicBase.quickUrl())\n    }\n    const enabled = value.enabled\n    if (!enabled) {\n      service.stop()\n      // The tunnel branch above follows the plan, not the master switch, so an\n      // explicit \"off\" must also drop the public ingress it started: otherwise\n      // the cloudflared child keeps a live public URL (and the relay keeps its\n      // stable row) while the panel says remote control is stopped. The relay\n      // row is deliberately kept so re-enabling reuses the same origin.\n      tunnel.stop()\n      disposeRelayHalf()\n      publicBase.reset()\n    }\n    if (disposeRoutes === undefined && enabled) {\n      disposeRoutes = ctx.effect(\n        () => {\n          const disposers = [\n            ...routes.map(route => ctx.webServer.register(route)),\n            ...upgrades.map(route => ctx.webServer.registerUpgrade(route)),\n          ]\n          return () => { for (const dispose of disposers) dispose() }\n        },\n        'remote-web-ui: pairing routes',\n      )\n    } else if (disposeRoutes !== undefined && !enabled) {\n      disposeRoutes()\n      disposeRoutes = undefined\n    }\n    if (disposeSweep === undefined && enabled) {\n      disposeSweep = ctx.effect(\n        () => {\n          const timer = nodeSetInterval(() => { service.sweep() }, SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS)\n          timer.unref()\n          return () => { clearInterval(timer) }\n        },\n        'remote-web-ui: presence sweep',\n      )\n    } else if (disposeSweep !== undefined && !enabled) {\n      disposeSweep()\n      disposeSweep = undefined\n    }\n    // Settings changed the reachable posture (manual publicBaseUrl, bind):\n    // re-probe unless the target set is unchanged.\n    runPostureProbe()\n  }\n  // Inject the crypto.randomUUID polyfill before any other script runs, so that\n  // the main bundle doesn't crash on non-secure contexts (LAN HTTP)\n  ctx.effect(() => ctx.on('webserver/index-inject', (table) => {\n    table.push({ kind: 'script', placement: 'head', text: UUID_POLYFILL_SCRIPT })\n  }), 'remote-web-ui: uuid polyfill')\n\n  // Issue #987: the browser-half channel patch installs at this plugin's\n  // boot entry, but dsh-client-connection boots earlier and opens its event\n  // streams unrewritten — on a non-loopback origin the SDK fence rejects\n  // them and the workspace list never loads. Contribute the rewrite as a\n  // parse-time head script so it is active before ANY boot entry runs; the\n  // client apply adopts the installed seat instead of patching twice. The\n  // row follows the live steady-state decision (enabled + pairing gate); the\n  // script itself skips loopback origins.\n  ctx.effect(() => ctx.on('webserver/index-inject', (table) => {\n    const value = resolve()\n    if (!value.enabled || !value.requirePairingForLan) return\n    table.push({ kind: 'script', placement: 'head', text: REMOTE_CHANNEL_BOOT_SCRIPT })\n  }), 'remote-web-ui: remote channel boot patch')\n\n  // The settings write path. The Host commits the new values into this row's\n  // volatile references and announces it here instead of remounting the row, so\n  // `sync` is what re-applies them: it re-reads every field through those\n  // references (see `resolve`) and is idempotent, so a save that changes\n  // nothing observable is a no-op while a disable, a bind flip or a tunnel\n  // change lands on the live instance without dropping the pairing service,\n  // its device sessions or the route registrations.\n  ctx.on('loader/volatile-update', () => { sync() })\n\n  // No settings registration: the Host derives this plugin's settings page\n  // from the exported `Config` schema, whose volatile fields are what make the\n  // page writable and what route a save through the live path above.\n  sync()\n}\n"

      "path": "packages/dsh-remote-web-ui/src/inner-auth.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * The inner browser credential for the remote desktop channel. The proxied\n * /api re-issues requests to 127.0.0.1, where the connection plugin's route\n * enforces the harness browser-auth cookie — an authority-bound signed cookie\n * with no loopback exemption on this cohort line, so a cookie minted for the\n * device's own authority can never satisfy the inner check. The process\n * therefore redeems its own launch token (the same one-time exchange every\n * paired device's first navigation performs) and attaches the resulting\n * cookie to inner requests. The credential is only ever exercised behind the\n * pairing gate: the `/remote` channel always requires a live paired-device\n * credential before this module is consulted, regardless of the\n * requirePairingForLan LAN policy (issue #1665).\n */\n\n/** Browser-auth credential the proxy attaches to loopback-bound requests. */\nexport interface InnerAuth {\n  /**\n   * Resolve the `name=value` cookie pair for inner requests, or undefined\n   * when the launch token is unavailable (the proxy then sends without a\n   * credential and the inner route answers 401, exactly as before).\n   */\n  ready(): Promise<string | undefined>\n  /** Drop the cached credential; the next ready() re-redeems. */\n  invalidate(): void\n}\n\n/** The harness browser-auth cookie name prefix (see dsh-client-connection). */\nconst BROWSER_AUTH_COOKIE_PREFIX = 'dsh-auth-'\n\n/**\n * Build the inner-auth handle.\n * @param launchUrl - the launch-token URL for the inner loopback authority\n *   (the connection service's authenticatedUrl of `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`),\n *   or undefined when the connection service or port is unavailable.\n * @param fetchImpl - injectable fetch (tests).\n */\nexport function createInnerAuth(\n  launchUrl: () => string | undefined,\n  fetchImpl: typeof fetch = fetch,\n): InnerAuth {\n  let cached: string | undefined\n  let inflight: Promise<string | undefined> | undefined\n\n  const redeem = async (): Promise<string | undefined> => {\n    const url = launchUrl()\n    if (url === undefined) return undefined\n    try {\n      // redirect: 'manual' keeps the 303's set-cookie readable instead of\n      // following it; the exchange itself is a plain GET with the token in\n      // the query, exactly what a first browser visit performs.\n      const response = await fetchImpl(url, { redirect: 'manual' })\n      const raw = response.headers.get('set-cookie')\n      if (raw === null) return undefined\n      // Generated cookie values are base64url and never contain commas, so a\n      // comma split followed by a prefix match finds the browser-auth entry\n      // even when the exchange sets several cookies.\n      const entry = raw\n        .split(',')\n        .map((part) => part.trim())\n        .find((part) => part.startsWith(BROWSER_AUTH_COOKIE_PREFIX))\n      if (entry === undefined) return undefined\n      const pair = entry.split(';')[0]?.trim()\n      return pair !== undefined && pair.includes('=') ? pair : undefined\n    } catch {\n      return undefined\n    }\n  }\n\n  return {\n    ready(): Promise<string | undefined> {\n      if (cached !== undefined) return Promise.resolve(cached)\n      inflight ??= redeem().then((value) => {\n        if (value !== undefined) cached = value\n        inflight = undefined\n        return value\n      }, () => {\n        inflight = undefined\n        return undefined\n      })\n      return inflight\n    },\n    invalidate(): void {\n      cached = undefined\n    },\n  }\n}\n"
