      "path": "packages/dsh-remote-web-ui/src/lan-bind-plan.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Pure decision helpers shared by the lan-bind sync path (index.ts) and the\n * status path (lanBindStatus). Extracted so the LAN-edge plan and the firewall\n * re-apply gate have one implementation and direct unit coverage.\n *\n * Since issue #1917 the plugin owns no bind: the host stays on loopback and LAN\n * reachability comes from the forwarder in lan-forward.ts, so the only decision\n * left here is which LAN address (if any) that forwarder may listen on.\n */\n\nimport { isLoopbackBind } from './host-bind-capability.ts'\n\n/** webStartup facts the CLI hands the process (absent unless a flag was passed). */\nexport interface StartupFacts {\n  host?: string\n  port?: number\n}\n\n/**\n * What the running host accepts, and which concrete addresses it could pin.\n * Sampled once per boot: the webserver package cannot change under a running\n * process, and the interface list is frozen for the same reason the QR bases\n * are (see src/lan.ts).\n */\nexport interface LanBindCapability {\n  /** Whether the installed webserver schema accepts the wildcard bind (reported, never written). */\n  wildcardSupported: boolean\n  /** Local non-loopback IPv4 literals, in preference order (`lanIPv4Addresses()`). */\n  candidates: string[]\n}\n\n/** Why the LAN forwarder is not listening, when it is not. */\nexport type ForwardStopReason =\n  /** The toggle is off (or was never flipped). */\n  | 'off'\n  /** The host itself binds a non-loopback address (`--host`): the forwarder yields the port. */\n  | 'host-bind'\n  /** The toggle is on but this machine has no LAN IPv4 address to listen on. */\n  | 'no-address'\n\n/** The LAN edge one sync should run: an address to listen on, or why not. */\nexport interface ForwardPlan {\n  /** The LAN address the forwarder listens on; undefined when it must stay off. */\n  host: string | undefined\n  /** Why it stays off; undefined when a host is planned. */\n  reason: ForwardStopReason | undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * The LAN address the forwarder may listen on, or the reason it must not.\n *\n * The order is: the toggle off keeps LAN off; a non-loopback `--host` means the\n * operator asked the HOST to bind the network itself, so the forwarder yields\n * the port instead of fighting it for the same address:port (issue #1917);\n * otherwise this machine's first LAN candidate. A host with no LAN IPv4 address\n * has nothing to listen on, which the caller reports instead of failing.\n *\n * Only a concrete interface address is ever returned: the wildcard would\n * collide with the loopback listener on the same port, and a forwarder bound to\n * `0.0.0.0` would additionally answer the loopback port a second time.\n * @param lanBind - the toggle value.\n * @param startupHost - the CLI-provided bind host, when given.\n * @param capability - the sampled interface candidates.\n * @returns the address to listen on, or the reason there is none.\n */\nexport function forwardPlanOf(\n  lanBind: boolean | undefined,\n  startupHost: string | undefined,\n  capability: LanBindCapability,\n): ForwardPlan {\n  if (lanBind !== true) return { host: undefined, reason: 'off' }\n  if (typeof startupHost === 'string' && startupHost !== '' && isLanReachableBind(startupHost)) {\n    return { host: undefined, reason: 'host-bind' }\n  }\n  const host = capability.candidates[0]\n  return host === undefined ? { host: undefined, reason: 'no-address' } : { host, reason: undefined }\n}\n\n/**\n * The reachability decision behind the QR bases, the status `lanUrls`, the\n * firewall summary and the boot's LAN warning: a bind that is not loopback is\n * reachable from another device, whatever literal it names. Equality with the\n * wildcard is deliberately not the test - on a host that refuses wildcard\n * binds the only LAN bind is a concrete interface address.\n * @param host - the block host or the live bind (absent before it settles).\n * @returns true when another device could dial the listener.\n */\nexport function isLanReachableBind(host: string | undefined): boolean {\n  return !isLoopbackBind(host)\n}\n\n/** The last firewall state this process applied. */\nexport interface AppliedFirewallState {\n  enabled: boolean\n  port: number\n}\n\n/** The managed profile when neither the config nor the runtime names one. */\nexport const DEFAULT_MANAGED_PROFILE = 'web'\n\n/**\n * The profile whose `cordis.patch.yml` the LAN bind toggle manages. An\n * explicit `profile` config wins; otherwise the launched profile the Host\n * publishes is authoritative, because the DSH Desktop client boots the\n * `desktop` profile without exporting `DSH_PROFILE` — an environment-only\n * fallback edited `profiles/web` there, so the toggle looked applied while\n * the running host never followed the block.\n * @param configured - the explicit `profile` plugin config, when set.\n * @param launched - the launched profile name the Host published, when available.\n * @param env - the DSH_PROFILE environment value, when set.\n */\nexport function resolveManagedProfile(\n  configured: string | undefined,\n  launched: string | undefined,\n  env: string | undefined,\n): string {\n  return configured ?? launched ?? env ?? DEFAULT_MANAGED_PROFILE\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether the firewall rule must be (re)applied: only when the toggle or the\n * bound port moved since the last application. Keeps unrelated settings\n * saves from spawning netsh/firewall-cmd delete+add churn.\n * @param previous - the state applied earlier by this process, if any.\n * @param next - the state the settings now ask for, if derivable.\n */\nexport function firewallActionNeeded(\n  previous: AppliedFirewallState | undefined,\n  next: AppliedFirewallState | undefined,\n): boolean {\n  if (next === undefined) return false\n  if (previous === undefined) return true\n  return previous.enabled !== next.enabled || previous.port !== next.port\n}\n"

      "path": "packages/dsh-remote-web-ui/src/lan-forward.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * The LAN edge the lan-bind toggle owns (issue #1917).\n *\n * The toggle used to pin the LAN address into the profile's webserver row. That\n * row is the only place the harness takes its bind from, and rewriting it\n *   - replaced the official row's whole config (so the row's own\n *     `host: !!js ctx.webStartup.host ?? '127.0.0.1'` expression and the CLI\n *     `--host`/`--port` never reached it), and\n *   - the profile patch is watched by the Host's HMR config watcher, so the\n *     write recomposed the running process and rebound the live listener.\n *\n * This module keeps the host bound to loopback and gives LAN clients their own\n * listener: a forwarder on the machine's LAN address, on the same port, that\n * re-issues every request (HTTP and WebSocket upgrade alike) to\n * `127.0.0.1:<port>`. Two consequences are load-bearing:\n *\n * 1. The upstream leg is loopback, so the socket alone would read as \"the\n *    desktop\". The forwarder therefore DROPS whatever Host the client sent and\n *    stamps the LAN authority it was reached at, plus `X-Forwarded-For`. Every\n *    fence that decides \"is this the desktop\" (`isLoopbackClient`, the pairing\n *    gate, the `/remote` gate) then keeps refusing the forwarded request, while\n *    the phone-facing fences still match the LAN authority the QR advertises.\n * 2. A bind that cannot be taken (address gone after a network change, port\n *    taken) only loses the LAN edge: the loopback listener is never touched, so\n *    the host cannot be bricked and the failure is reported on the status\n *    frame.\n *\n * Nothing here writes a file: the forwarder is runtime state, so a network\n * change needs no profile edit and no restart.\n *\n * @module @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui/lan-forward\n */\n\nimport { createServer, request as httpRequest, type ClientRequest, type IncomingMessage, type Server, type ServerResponse } from 'node:http'\nimport { connect } from 'node:net'\nimport type { Duplex } from 'node:stream'\n\n/** The upstream the forwarder re-issues to: the process's own loopback listener. */\nexport const FORWARD_UPSTREAM_HOST = '127.0.0.1'\n\n/**\n * Headers that describe one hop rather than the request. They are rebuilt for\n * each leg so a keep-alive or upgrade marker from the client never leaks into\n * the loopback leg (and vice versa on the response).\n */\nconst HOP_BY_HOP = new Set([\n  'connection',\n  'keep-alive',\n  'proxy-authenticate',\n  'proxy-authorization',\n  'proxy-connection',\n  'te',\n  'trailer',\n  'transfer-encoding',\n  'upgrade',\n])\n\n/**\n * Headers the forwarder owns: a client-supplied value is discarded, never\n * appended to, so a LAN client cannot claim to be the desktop by forging them.\n */\nconst REWRITTEN = new Set(['host', 'x-forwarded-for', 'x-forwarded-proto', 'x-forwarded-host', 'cf-connecting-ip'])\n\n/** What the forwarder is doing right now, for the status frame and the logs. */\nexport interface LanForwardState {\n  /** Whether the LAN listener is bound. */\n  listening: boolean\n  /** The LAN address it listens on (undefined when it never bound). */\n  address: string | undefined\n  /** The port it listens on (the web server's own port). */\n  port: number | undefined\n  /** The loopback port it re-issues to. */\n  upstreamPort: number | undefined\n  /** Why the last bind attempt failed, when it did. */\n  error: string | undefined\n}\n\n/** The idle state: nothing bound, nothing failed. */\nexport const IDLE_FORWARD_STATE: LanForwardState = {\n  listening: false,\n  address: undefined,\n  port: undefined,\n  upstreamPort: undefined,\n  error: undefined,\n}\n\n/**\n * The `Host` authority a listener at `address:port` is reached at. IPv6\n * literals are bracketed like any URL authority.\n * @param address - the listen address (a literal).\n * @param port - the listen port.\n * @returns the authority text a request to that listener carries.\n */\nexport function authorityOf(address: string, port: number): string {\n  const host = address.includes(':') ? `[${address}]` : address\n  return `${host}:${String(port)}`\n}\n\n/**\n * The headers the loopback leg carries for one request: the client's own\n * headers minus the hop-by-hop and forwarder-owned ones, plus the LAN authority\n * the client actually reached and its address.\n * @param request - the request as it arrived on the LAN listener.\n * @param authority - the LAN authority the forwarder listens at.\n * @param clientAddress - the client's socket address, when readable.\n * @returns the headers for the loopback request.\n */\nexport function forwardedHeaders(\n  request: IncomingMessage,\n  authority: string,\n  clientAddress: string | undefined,\n): Record<string, string> {\n  const headers: Record<string, string> = {}\n  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(request.headers)) {\n    if (value === undefined) continue\n    const lower = name.toLowerCase()\n    if (HOP_BY_HOP.has(lower) || REWRITTEN.has(lower)) continue\n    headers[lower] = Array.isArray(value) ? value.join(', ') : value\n  }\n  headers.host = authority\n  if (clientAddress !== undefined && clientAddress !== '') headers['x-forwarded-for'] = clientAddress\n  headers['x-forwarded-proto'] = 'http'\n  return headers\n}\n\n/**\n * Rebuild a WebSocket handshake for the loopback leg. The client's own headers\n * travel through verbatim (so `Sec-WebSocket-*` and any application protocol\n * survive) except the ones the forwarder owns.\n * @param request - the upgrade request as it arrived on the LAN listener.\n * @param authority - the LAN authority the forwarder listens at.\n * @param clientAddress - the client's socket address, when readable.\n * @returns the handshake request head to write on the loopback leg.\n */\nexport function forwardedHandshake(\n  request: IncomingMessage,\n  authority: string,\n  clientAddress: string | undefined,\n): string {\n  const lines = [`${request.method ?? 'GET'} ${request.url ?? '/'} HTTP/1.1`]\n  const raw = request.rawHeaders\n  for (let index = 0; index + 1 < raw.length; index += 2) {\n    const name = raw[index] ?? ''\n    const lower = name.toLowerCase()\n    if (REWRITTEN.has(lower)) continue\n    lines.push(`${name}: ${raw[index + 1] ?? ''}`)\n  }\n  lines.push(`Host: ${authority}`)\n  if (clientAddress !== undefined && clientAddress !== '') lines.push(`X-Forwarded-For: ${clientAddress}`)\n  lines.push('X-Forwarded-Proto: http')\n  return `${lines.join('\\r\\n')}\\r\\n\\r\\n`\n}\n\n/** One listener, its live connections, and its last bind outcome. */\nexport class LanForwarder {\n  private server: Server | undefined\n  private config: { address: string; port: number; upstreamPort: number } | undefined\n  private state: LanForwardState = IDLE_FORWARD_STATE\n  /** Every socket this forwarder opened on either leg. */\n  private readonly sockets = new Set<Duplex>()\n  /** Every in-flight loopback request, so a teardown cannot leave one running. */\n  private readonly upstreams = new Set<ClientRequest>()\n\n  /** What the forwarder is doing right now. */\n  snapshot(): LanForwardState {\n    return this.state\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Bind the LAN listener, or report why it could not be bound.\n   *\n   * Never throws: a bind failure is the ordinary outcome after a network change\n   * (the address is gone) or a port collision, and the loopback listener must\n   * keep serving regardless.\n   * @param address - the LAN address to listen on.\n   * @param port - the port to listen on (the web server's own port).\n   * @param upstreamPort - the loopback port to re-issue to; defaults to `port`.\n   * @returns the settled state.\n   */\n  start(address: string, port: number, upstreamPort: number = port): Promise<LanForwardState> {\n    if (this.config !== undefined && this.state.listening\n      && this.config.address === address && this.config.port === port && this.config.upstreamPort === upstreamPort) {\n      return Promise.resolve(this.state)\n    }\n    return this.stop().then(() => this.bind(address, port, upstreamPort))\n  }\n\n  private bind(address: string, port: number, upstreamPort: number): Promise<LanForwardState> {\n    // The authority the requests are stamped with; re-read after listen so a\n    // kernel-assigned port (or a resolved address) is what clients are told.\n    let authority = authorityOf(address, port)\n    const server = createServer((request, response) => { this.forwardHttp(request, response, upstreamPort, authority) })\n    server.on('upgrade', (request, socket, head) => { this.forwardUpgrade(request, socket, head, upstreamPort, authority) })\n    server.on('connection', (socket) => {\n      this.sockets.add(socket)\n      socket.on('close', () => { this.sockets.delete(socket) })\n    })\n    this.server = server\n    this.config = { address, port, upstreamPort }\n    return new Promise<LanForwardState>((resolve) => {\n      let settled = false\n      const settle = (next: LanForwardState): void => {\n        if (settled) return\n        settled = true\n        this.state = next\n        resolve(next)\n      }\n      // A failed bind arrives as an 'error' event (EADDRINUSE, EADDRNOTAVAIL, a\n      // permission refusal). It is reported, never re-thrown: an unhandled\n      // 'error' on a listening server would take the whole host process down.\n      server.on('error', (error: NodeJS.ErrnoException) => {\n        const reason = error.code === undefined ? error.message : `${error.code}: ${error.message}`\n        if (this.server === server) {\n          this.server = undefined\n          this.config = undefined\n        }\n        this.releaseSockets()\n        settle({ listening: false, address, port, upstreamPort, error: reason })\n        if (!server.listening) return\n        server.close(() => undefined)\n      })\n      server.listen(port, address, () => {\n        // Report the address and port the kernel actually bound: a port of 0\n        // (and a wildcard-adjacent literal) is resolved by the listen call, and\n        // the status frame must name the listener clients can dial.\n        const bound = server.address()\n        const boundPort = typeof bound === 'object' && bound !== null ? bound.port : port\n        const boundAddress = typeof bound === 'object' && bound !== null ? bound.address : address\n        authority = authorityOf(boundAddress, boundPort)\n        this.config = { address: boundAddress, port: boundPort, upstreamPort }\n        settle({ listening: true, address: boundAddress, port: boundPort, upstreamPort, error: undefined })\n      })\n    })\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Close the LAN listener and every connection it opened, then resolve once the\n   * port is released. Safe to call when nothing is bound.\n   */\n  stop(): Promise<void> {\n    const server = this.server\n    this.server = undefined\n    this.config = undefined\n    this.releaseSockets()\n    this.state = IDLE_FORWARD_STATE\n    if (server === undefined) return Promise.resolve()\n    return new Promise<void>((resolve) => {\n      server.close(() => { resolve() })\n      // Keep-alive and upgraded connections keep the handle alive; they are\n      // already destroyed above, so the close above settles on the next tick.\n      server.closeAllConnections?.()\n    })\n  }\n\n  private releaseSockets(): void {\n    for (const upstream of this.upstreams) upstream.destroy()\n    this.upstreams.clear()\n    for (const socket of this.sockets) socket.destroy()\n    this.sockets.clear()\n  }\n\n  private trackUpstream(upstream: ClientRequest): void {\n    this.upstreams.add(upstream)\n    upstream.on('close', () => { this.upstreams.delete(upstream) })\n  }\n\n  private forwardHttp(request: IncomingMessage, response: ServerResponse, upstreamPort: number, authority: string): void {\n    const upstream = httpRequest({\n      host: FORWARD_UPSTREAM_HOST,\n      port: upstreamPort,\n      method: request.method,\n      path: request.url,\n      headers: forwardedHeaders(request, authority, request.socket.remoteAddress),\n    }, (upstreamResponse) => {\n      const headers: Record<string, string | string[]> = {}\n      for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(upstreamResponse.headers)) {\n        if (value === undefined || HOP_BY_HOP.has(name.toLowerCase())) continue\n        headers[name] = value\n      }\n      response.writeHead(upstreamResponse.statusCode ??       "content": "/**\n * Loopback-shaped reverse proxy used by the remote desktop channel: after\n * the pairing cookie gate, traffic is re-issued to 127.0.0.1 so sibling\n * plugin fences (socket + Host loopback) accept it. Origin, cookies, and\n * caller-controlled Sec-Fetch markers are dropped, and HTTP requests receive\n * a synthetic same-origin marker so sibling loopback routes that require a\n * browser tripwire accept the authenticated proxy.\n *\n * Every other request header is forwarded unchanged, because a plugin may\n * authenticate its own calls with a header of its own: an allowlist here\n * silently dropped those markers and made the plugin refuse every remote\n * write request (issue #1925).\n */\n\nimport type { IncomingMessage, OutgoingHttpHeaders, ServerResponse } from 'node:http'\nimport { request as httpRequest } from 'node:http'\nimport { connect } from 'node:net'\nimport type { Duplex } from 'node:stream'\nimport { writeJson } from './http.ts'\nimport type { InnerAuth } from './inner-auth.ts'\n\n/** WebSocket handshake headers forwarded to the loopback upstream. */\nconst WS_FORWARD_HEADERS = [\n  'sec-websocket-key',\n  'sec-websocket-version',\n  'sec-websocket-extensions',\n  'sec-websocket-protocol',\n] as const\n\n/**\n * Request headers the re-issue never carries: hop-by-hop headers (RFC 9110\n * 7.6.1), the ones this proxy owns or rewrites, the forwarding marks of a hop\n * that stood in between, and the browser fetch metadata that describes the\n * caller's own request. Everything else is passed through, so a plugin that\n * authenticates its calls with a header of its own keeps working behind the\n * pairing gate (issue #1925).\n *\n * The forwarding marks (x-forwarded-*, cf-connecting-ip, forwarded) must not\n * ride along: the re-issued request is a loopback one, and an edge stamp would\n * make the local fences classify it as remote and refuse every route\n * (shared/host/loopback.ts owns that rule). x-dsh-remote-device is the\n * caller's own live device credential: the channel consumes it at its gate and\n * never hands it further, the same way compressed or partial body could never be described to the caller.\n */\nconst REQUEST_HEADER_DENYLIST = new Set([\n  // hop-by-hop\n  'connection',\n  'keep-alive',\n  'proxy-authenticate',\n  'proxy-authorization',\n  'expect',\n  'te',\n  'trailer',\n  'transfer-encoding',\n  'upgrade',\n  // rewritten by this proxy: the loopback authority and the tripwire marker\n  'host',\n  'sec-fetch-site',\n  // the caller's own origin, its cookie jar, and the credential the gate consumed\n  'origin',\n  'referer',\n  'cookie',\n  'x-dsh-remote-device',\n  // forwarding marks: a re-issued request is loopback, not forwarded\n  'forwarded',\n  'x-forwarded-for',\n  'x-forwarded-host',\n  'x-forwarded-port',\n  'x-forwarded-proto',\n  'x-real-ip',\n  'cf-connecting-ip',\n  // response shaping (see the doc comment above): these ask the upstream for a\n  // body the copied response headers cannot describe\n  'accept-encoding',\n  'range',\n  'if-range',\n])\n\n/**\n * Prefixes the re-issue never carries: the browser fetch metadata\n * (sec-fetch-*, sec-ch-*) describes the outer request, not this one.\n */\nconst REQUEST_HEADER_DENY_PREFIXES = ['sec-']\n\n/**\n * Header names the caller nominated as hop-by-hop through its own Connection\n * header (RFC 9110 7.6.1): whatever it names stops at this proxy too.\n * @param connection - the outer request Connection header value.\n * @returns the nominated names, lowercased.\n */\nfunction nominatedHeaders(connection: string | string[] | undefined): Set<string> {\n  const nominated = new Set<string>()\n  if (connection === undefined) return nominated\n  for (const value of Array.isArray(connection) ? connection : [connection]) {\n    for (const token of value.split(',')) {\n      const name = token.trim().toLowerCase()\n      if (name !== '') nominated.add(name)\n    }\n  }\n  return nominated\n}\n\n/**\n * Headers of the loopback re-issue: the caller headers minus the ones the\n * channel owns, plus the rewritten authority, the synthetic same-origin\n * tripwire, and the inner credential that replaces the caller cookie.\n * @param req - the already-gated outer request.\n * @param port - local webServer port.\n * @param cookie - the inner credential, when one resolved.\n * @returns headers to send to 127.0.0.1.\n */\nfunction forwardedRequestHeaders(req: IncomingMessage, port: number, cookie: string | undefined): Record<string, string> {\n  const nominated = nominatedHeaders(req.headers.connection)\n  const headers: Record<string, string> = {}\n  for (let index = 0; index + 1 < req.rawHeaders.length; index += 2) {\n    const name = req.rawHeaders[index].toLowerCase()\n    if (REQUEST_HEADER_DENYLIST.has(name) || nominated.has(name)) continue\n    if upstream as one comma-joined value, the same\n    // way node folds duplicates on the receiving side.\n    headers[name] = previous === undefined ? value : `${previous}, ${value}`\n  }\n  headers.host {\n  const headers = forwardedRequestHeaders(req, port, cookie)\n\n  const upstream = httpRequest({\n    host: '127.0.0.1',\n    port,\n    path: upstreamPath,\n    method: req.method,\n    headers,\n  }, (upstreamRes) => {\n    // The cached credential went stale (secret rotation, credential store\n    // reset): drop it so the next request re-redeems. Guarded so a normal completion never destroys a\n    // keep-alive socket the agent would reuse.\n    res.on('close', () => {\n      if (!upstreamRes.readableEnded) upstream.destroy()\n    })\n  })\n  upstream.on('error', () => {\n    if (!res.headersSent) {\n      writeJson(res, 502, { ok: false, error: { code: 'upstream-failure', message: 'upstream request failed' } })\n      return\n    }\n    res.destroy()\n  })\n  // The outer request aborted mid-body: reset the inner request instead of\n  // feeding it a truncated body that still gets processed (mirror of the\n  // upgrade path's two-leg teardown).\n  req.on('error', () => { upstream.destroy() })\n  req.pipe(upstream)\n}\n\n/**\n * Rebuild a WebSocket handshake as loopback-shaped and pipe both directions.\n * @param req - the already-gated upgrade request.\n * @param socket - the client duplex.\n * @param head - bytes already read past the handshake.\n * @param port - local webServer port.\n * @param upstreamPath - path + query on 127.0.0.1.\n * @param cookie - the inner browser-auth credential for the handshake, when\n *   the upstream route enforces it (the gateway event-stream mux does).\n */\nexport function proxyLoopbackUpgrade(\n  req: IncomingMessage,\n  socket: Duplex,\n  head: Buffer,\n  port: number,\n  upstreamPath: string,\n  cookie?: string,\n): void {\n  const lines = [\n    `GET ${upstreamPath} HTTP/1.1`,\n    `Host: 127.0.0.1:${String(port)}`,\n    'Upgrade: websocket',\n    'Connection: Upgrade',\n  ]\n  if (cookie !== undefined) lines.push(`Cookie: ${cookie}`)\n  for (const name of WS_FORWARD_HEADERS) {\n    const value = req.headers[name]\n    if (value === undefined) continue\n    lines.push(`${name}: ${Array.isArray(value) ? value.join(', ') : value}`)\n  }\n  const handshake = `${lines.join('\\r\\n')}\\r\\n\\r\\n`\n\n  const upstream = connect(port, '127.0.0.1')\n  // A half-open tunnel path (dead-but-alive edge connection) would otherwise\n  // let the phone's mux socket sit stale for minutes: keepalive probes the\n  // pipe periodically and destroys both legs on the first real gap, so the\n  // client's reconnect + stream re-baseline re-syncs the feed in seconds.\n  ;(socket as unknown as import('node:net').Socket).setKeepAlive(true, 20_000)\n  upstream.setKeepAlive(true, 20_000)\n  const tearDown = (): void => {\n    upstream.destroy()\n    socket.destroy()\n  }\n  upstream.on('error', tearDown)\n  socket.on('error', tearDown)\n  upstream.on('close', () => { socket.destroy() })\n  socket.on('close', () => { upstream.destroy() })\n  upstream.on('connect', () => {\n    upstream.write(handshake)\n    if (head.length > 0) upstream.write(head)\n    socket.pipe(upstream)\n    upstream.pipe(socket)\n  })\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * One-time pairing grants for the /pair-app landing.\n *\n * The QR entry (`/pair-accept?pair=<token>`) used to hand the freshly minted\n * device id to the app landing in its own URL (`/pair-app?device=<id>`). A\n * device id is a live session credential: the channel gate authorizes every\n * gated request by it and the cookie it mirrors lives a year, so a URL carrying\n * it leaks that credential into browser history, the address bar, and every log\n * on the path. The landing is reached with a one-time grant instead — 256 bits\n * of entropy, a short TTL, and single-consume semantics — and the device id\n * reaches the client only inside the server-rendered shell (the capture script\n * the landing patches in).\n *\n * Consume semantics follow the reference implementation's one-time host\n * capability (zcode `packages/server/src/hostCapability.ts`): the record is\n * deleted on EVERY consume attempt — success, expiry, or replay — so a captured\n * grant is worthless after its first use and a replayed one can never resolve,\n * and only a first use inside the TTL yields a device.\n *\n * @module @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui/pair-grant\n */\n\nimport { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto'\n\n/**\n * Default grant lifetime. The grant only has to survive one redirect chain\n * from the accept page to the app landing, tunnel round trips included, so it\n * is far shorter than the device session it stands in for.\n */\nexport const DEFAULT_PAIR_GRANT_TTL_MS = 60_000\n\n/**\n * Cap on live grants. The accept page is rate-limited per source, but the\n * table is still caller-driven, so it stays bounded (oldest evicted first)\n * exactly like the device table.\n */\nexport const MAX_LIVE_GRANTS = 256\n\n/** Clock/entropy injection for tests. */\nexport interface PairGrantStoreOptions {\n  /** Grant lifetime in ms (default {@link DEFAULT_PAIR_GRANT_TTL_MS}). */\n  ttlMs?: number\n  /** Clock seam (default Date.now). */\n  now?: () => number\n  /** Entropy seam (default 32 random bytes, base64url). */\n  createGrant?: () => string\n}\n\n/** One issued grant and its absolute expiry (both non-secret to the issuer). */\nexport interface PairGrantRecord {\n  /** The one-time secret carried in the /pair-app URL. */\n  grant: string\n  /** Absolute expiry (ms epoch); a consume past this resolves to nothing. */\n  expiresAt: number\n}\n\n/** The grant table surface the routes consume. */\nexport interface PairGrantStore {\n  /** Mint one grant bound to a device session. */\n  issue(deviceId: string): PairGrantRecord\n  /** Redeem a grant once, returning its device id (undefined when unusable). */\n  consume(grant: string | undefined): string | undefined\n  /** Liveness check that does not spend the grant (the fence fallback). */\n  peek(grant: string | undefined): string | undefined\n  /** Live grant count (tests/diagnostics). */\n  readonly size: number\n}\n\n/** One live grant. */\ninterface GrantEntry {\n  deviceId: string\n  expiresAt: number\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the grant table. Pure TypeScript with injected clock/randomness so the\n * whole one-time semantics are unit-testable without a server.\n */\nexport function createPairGrantStore(options: PairGrantStoreOptions = {}): PairGrantStore {\n  const ttlMs = options.ttlMs ?? DEFAULT_PAIR_GRANT_TTL_MS\n  const now = options.now ?? ((): number => Date.now())\n  const createGrant = options.createGrant ?? ((): string => randomBytes(32).toString('base64url'))\n  const entries = new Map<string, GrantEntry>()\n\n  const purgeExpired = (at: number): void => {\n    for (const [grant, entry] of entries) {\n      if (entry.expiresAt <= at) entries.delete(grant)\n    }\n  }\n\n  return {\n    issue(deviceId: string): PairGrantRecord {\n      const issuedAt = now()\n      purgeExpired(issuedAt)\n      while (entries.size >= MAX_LIVE_GRANTS) {\n        const oldest = entries.keys().next().value\n        if (oldest === undefined) break\n        entries.delete(oldest)\n      }\n      const grant = createGrant()\n      const expiresAt = issuedAt + ttlMs\n      entries.set(grant, { deviceId, expiresAt })\n      return { grant, expiresAt }\n    },\n    consume(grant: string | undefined): string | undefined {\n      if (grant === undefined || grant === '') return undefined\n      const consumedAt = now()\n      const entry = entries.get(grant)\n      // Delete before validating: a replayed grant must never resolve, and an\n      // expired one must not linger in the table.\n      entries.delete(grant)\n      purgeExpired(consumedAt)\n      if (entry === undefined || entry.expiresAt <= consumedAt) return undefined\n      return entry.deviceId\n    },\n    peek(grant: string | undefined): string | undefined {\n      if (grant === undefined || grant === '') return undefined\n      const at = now()\n      const entry = entries.get(grant)\n      if (entry === undefined) return undefined\n      if (entry.expiresAt <= at) {\n        entries.delete(grant)\n        return undefined\n      }\n      return entry.deviceId\n    },\n    get size(): number {\n      return entries.size\n    },\n  }\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * Optional cordis service other host plugins can ctx.get without taking a\n * package dependency: a live paired-device cookie is an allow path on\n * routes that sit outside /api (and therefore outside api/gate).\n */\nimport type { IncomingMessage } from 'node:http'\nimport { Service, type Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'\n\n/** Named lookup key sibling plugins pass to ctx.get. */\nexport const REMOTE_WEB_UI_PAIRING = 'remoteWebUiPairing'\n\n/**\n * Pairing identity for one HTTP request. Structural: consumers must not\n * import this class, only the method shape.\n */\nexport class RemoteWebUiPairing extends Service {\n  /**\n   * @param ctx - host plugin context.\n   * @param check - live cookie + session predicate (re-read per request).\n   */\n  constructor(\n    ctx: Context,\n    private readonly check: (request: IncomingMessage) => boolean,\n  ) {\n    super(ctx, REMOTE_WEB_UI_PAIRING)\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Whether the request carries a live paired-device cookie.\n   * @param request - the incoming HTTP request.\n   * @returns true when the session is live and was refreshed.\n   */\n  isPairedDevice(request: IncomingMessage): boolean {\n    return this.check(request)\n  }\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * Pairing state machine: one active one-time token, a device-session table,\n * and presence tracking. The\n * cordis-facing surfaces (routes, the api/gate listener) live next door.\n *\n * Security invariants:\n * - One active token at a time; `issue()` replaces it, so a refreshed QR\n *   immediately invalidates the previous link.\n * - A token is a bearer credential for its whole window: it is refused only\n *   when unknown, expired, or after `stop()`, and the same link may pair\n *   repeatedly within that window (each accept mints a fresh device session).\n *   Mobile flows routinely split across cookie contexts (camera preview to\n *   in-app browser to the system browser), and the later context must be\n *   able to complete its own pairing from the same link.\n * - Tokens expire; `accept()` on an expired token is refused like an\n *   unknown one (no oracle for validity).\n * - `stop()` revokes every device session and clears the token, so paired\n *   devices are cut off on their next gated request.\n * - `revoke()` drops one device session; idle sessions older than\n *   `idleExpireMs` are deleted on sweep, load, and the next gated request.\n */\n\nimport { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto'\nimport { mkdirSync, readFileSync, renameSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'\nimport { dirname } from 'node:path'\nimport type { PostureHost, PostureSnapshot } from './posture.ts'\nimport { sameIngressFrame, type IngressSyncFrame } from './ingress-sync.ts'\n\n/** The observable pairing phases the panel renders. */\nexport type PairingPhase =\n  /** The server is not bound all-interfaces: no usable QR exists. */\n  | 'lan-required'\n  /** Remote control was stopped; a fresh QR (issue) re-enables it. */\n  | 'stopped'\n  /** A token is live and no device has paired with it yet. */\n  | 'waiting'\n  /** At least one paired device was active recently. */\n  | 'connected'\n  /** Devices are paired but none has been active within the offline window. */\n  | 'disconnected'\n\n/** One issued pairing token (keyed by its secret). */\nexport interface TokenRecord {\n  /** Monotonic issue time (ms epoch), drives refresh ordering. */\n  issuedAt: number\n  /** Absolute expiry (ms epoch); accept() past this is refused. */\n  expiresAt: number\n  /** Opaque, non-secret identifier surfaced in snapshots (never the pairing secret). */\n  id: string\n  /** Workspace the QR link should land the phone in (optional). */\n  workspaceId?: string\n  /** LAN IP literal the QR link was built from (optional; default first). */\n  address?: string\n}\n\n/**\n * Default idle-expiry window: 30 days without a heartbeat or a gated\n * request. The reopen service worker refreshes lastSeenAt on every\n * navigation it serves, so the window only runs out through genuine\n * disuse; 30 days matches the browser-credential lifetimes the surrounding\n * flow was built around, while the effective device lifetime stays shorter\n * than the 365-day cookie because of this sweep. Override per deployment\n * through the idleExpireMs config.\n */\nexport const DEFAULT_IDLE_EXPIRE_MS = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000\n\n/** Cap on the persisted/displayed User-Agent string. */\nconst MAX_USER_AGENT_CHARS = 180\n\n/** Cap on a user-defined device name. */\nconst MAX_DEVICE_NAME_CHARS = 64\n\n/** One paired device session, keyed by the device id stored in its cookie. */\nexport interface DeviceSession {\n  /** Pairing time (ms epoch). */\n  createdAt: number\n  /** Last time the device passed a gated request or heartbeat. */\n  lastSeenAt: number\n  /** Sanitized User-Agent captured at accept (optional; missing on old files). */\n  userAgent?: string\n  /**\n   * User-defined label shown instead of the User-Agent-derived name.       "content": "/**\n * The remote-channel rewrite contract as pure data (issue #987): both the\n * browser patch (client/remote-channel.ts) and the parse-time boot patch\n * (remote-channel-boot.ts, inlined into index.html by the host) decide from\n * these tables, so the two can never drift apart.\n * @module @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui/remote-channel-rules\n */\n\n/** The gated mirror prefix (must match src/remote-methods.ts). */\nexport const REMOTE_PREFIX = '/remote'\n\nimport { REMOTE_DEVICE_HEADER, REMOTE_DEVICE_QUERY } from './remote-methods.ts'\n\n/**\n * The schemes that can deliver a page a remote party controls: the network\n * transports, plus the documents a network page can mint.       "content": "/**\n * Pure planner for the settings-sync tunnel branch: given the resolved\n * settings slice, decide which tunnel mode runs and with what target. Kept\n * free of cordis types so the precedence matrix is unit-testable without a\n * host context.\n */\n\n/** Whether a configured public base is a parseable http(s) URL with a host. */\nexport function isHttpUrl(value: string): boolean {\n  try {\n    const url = new URL(value)\n    return (url.protocol === 'http:' || url.protocol === 'https:') && url.hostname !== ''\n  } catch {\n    return false\n  }\n}\n\n/** How the settings sync should drive the tunnel for one resolved value. */\nexport type TunnelPlan =\n  | { mode: 'off' }\n  | { mode: 'quick'; targetUrl: string; ignored: Array<'tunnelToken' | 'publicBaseUrl'> }\n  | { mode: 'named'; token: string; publicUrl: string }\n\n/**\n * Decide the tunnel mode and target from one resolved settings value.\n * Precedence: the quick tunnel wins when `autoTunnel` is on (anything else\n * configured is reported as ignored); the named tunnel runs only with a\n * token AND a valid public hostname (the token does not carry the hostname,\n * so the QR base and the fence trust would have no source without it);\n * otherwise no tunnel and the manual public base applies.\n *\n * The quick target URL names the local webServer port, so a plan made before\n * the listener binds cannot be quick: it comes back `off` and the caller —\n * which can observe the port settle — re-plans. The planner itself never\n * emits an `http://127.0.0.1:undefined` target.\n * @param value - the resolved settings slice that drives the tunnel.\n * @param port - the local webServer port the tunnel forwards to (undefined\n *   before the listener binds).\n */\nexport function tunnelPlanOf(\n  value: { autoTunnel?: boolean; tunnelToken?: string; publicBaseUrl?: string },\n  port: number | undefined,\n): TunnelPlan {\n  if (value.autoTunnel === true) {\n    if (port === undefined) return { mode: 'off' }\n    const ignored: Array<'tunnelToken' | 'publicBaseUrl'> = []\n    if (value.tunnelToken !== undefined && value.tunnelToken !== '') ignored.push('tunnelToken')\n    if (value.publicBaseUrl !== undefined && value.publicBaseUrl !== '') ignored.push('publicBaseUrl')\n    return { mode: 'quick', targetUrl: `http://127.0.0.1:${String(port)}`, ignored }\n  }\n  if (value.tunnelToken !== undefined && value.tunnelToken !== '') {\n    if (value.publicBaseUrl !== undefined && isHttpUrl(value.publicBaseUrl)) {\n      return { mode: 'named', token: value.tunnelToken, publicUrl: value.publicBaseUrl }\n    }\n    return { mode: 'off' }\n  }\n  return { mode: 'off' }\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * The SSH engine facade: a per-alias persistent connection pool (ssh2) with\n * multi-hop jump support, command execution, PTY shells, SFTP transfers,\n * local port-forward tunnels and cluster execution. The heavy lifting lives\n * in the engine/ modules (connection-pool, pty, sftp, tunnel, cluster); this\n * class composes them behind one new SshEngine instance per plugin apply.\n */\n\nimport type { ClusterResult, ExecResult, SshHostSummary, TestResult, TransferProgress, TunnelInfo } from './protocol.ts'\nimport type { HostStore } from './store.ts'\nimport {\n  DEFAULTS,\n  execCommand,\n  disposeRecord,\n  sweepPool,\n  type EngineOptions,\n  type KeyboardInteractiveHandler,\n  type PoolRecord,\n} from './engine/connection-pool.ts'\nimport { openShell, type ShellSession } from './engine/pty.ts'\nimport { download, ls, upload } from './engine/sftp.ts'\nimport { listTunnels, startTunnel, stopAllTunnels, stopTunnel, type TunnelRecord } from './engine/tunnel.ts'\nimport { cluster } from './engine/cluster.ts'\n\nexport type { EngineOptions, KeyboardInteractiveHandler } from './engine/connection-pool.ts'\nexport type { ShellSession } from './engine/pty.ts'\nexport type { PoolRecord } from './engine/connection-pool.ts'\nexport type { TunnelRecord } from './engine/tunnel.ts'\n\n/**\n * The engine. Owns the pool, tunnels, and all operations. One instance per\n * plugin apply; dispose() closes every connection.\n */\nexport class SshEngine {\n  readonly store: HostStore\n  readonly opts: Required<EngineOptions>\n  readonly pool = new Map<string, PoolRecord>()\n  readonly acquireQueue = new Map<string, Promise<PoolRecord>>()\n  readonly tunnels = new Map<string, TunnelRecord>()\n  nextTunnelId = 1\n  private sweepTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined\n\n  /**\n   * @param store - the host config store.\n   * @param options - engine knobs (defaults applied).\n   */\n  constructor(store: HostStore, options?: EngineOptions) {\n    this.store = store\n    this.opts = { ...DEFAULTS, ...options }\n    this.sweepTimer = setInterval(() => sweepPool(this), Math.max(10_000, this.opts.idleTimeoutMs / 4))\n    this.sweepTimer.unref?.()\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Change the pre-ready ceiling (TCP connect + key exchange + user\n   * authentication) for connections opened from now on. rows: number },\n  onKeyboardInteractive?: KeyboardInteractiveHandler,\n): Promise<ShellSession> {\n  const entry = engine.store.find(alias)\n  if (entry === undefined) throw new Error('alias \\'' + alias + '\\' not found — add it first')\n  const { client, hops } = await connectChain(engine, entry, onKeyboardInteractive)\n  return await new Promise<ShellSession>((resolve, reject) => {\n    client.shell({ term: 'xterm-256color', cols: size.cols, rows: size.rows }, (error, stream) => {\n      if (error !== undefined) {\n        try { client.end() } catch { /* closed */ }\n        for (const hop of hops) { try { hop.end() } catch { /* closed */ } }\n        reject(error)\n        return\n      }\n      let tornDown = false\n      const teardown = (): void => {\n        if (tornDown) return\n        tornDown = true\n        try { client.end() } catch { /* closed */ }\n        for (const hop of hops) { try { hop.end() } catch { /* closed */ } }\n      }\n      const session: ShellSession = {\n        send: (data) => { try { stream.write(data) } catch { /* channel gone */ } },\n        resize: (cols, rows) => { try { stream.setWindow(rows, cols, rows, cols) } catch { /* channel gone */ } },\n        close: () => {\n          try { stream.close() } catch { /* channel gone */ }\n          teardown()\n        },\n        pause: () => { try { stream.pause() } catch { /* channel gone */ } },\n        resume: () => { try { stream.resume() } catch { /* channel gone */ } },\n      }\n      stream.on('data', (chunk: Buffer) => { session.onData?.(chunk) })\n      stream.on('close', (code: number | null) => {\n        teardown()\n        session.onExit?.(code)\n      })\n      stream.on('error', (streamError: Error) => {\n        teardown()\n        session.onExit?.(null, streamError instanceof Error ? streamError.message : String(streamError))\n      })\n      resolve(session)\n    })\n  })\n}"

      "content": "/**\n * Host-side terminal sessions for the web terminal.\n *\n * The PTY shell is owned here, not by the browser view: a view can detach\n * (panel switch, page unmount, a dropped socket) and reattach by session id\n * without tearing the remote shell down, which is what makes the terminal\n * survival property the old DOM takeover used to provide. A session with no\n * attached socket is reaped after an idle window, and an exited one is kept\n * for a short grace window so a reattaching view still sees the final screen.\n */\nimport { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto'\nimport { WebSocket } from 'ws'\nimport type { KeyboardInteractiveHandler } from './connection-pool.ts'\nimport type { ShellSession } from './pty.ts'\nimport type { TerminalServerFrame } from '../protocol.ts'\n\n/** Pause the shell when an attached socket's send buffer exceeds this… */\nconst BACKPRESSURE_HIGH_WATER = 1024 * 1024\n\n/** …and resume once every attached socket drains below this. */\nconst BACKPRESSURE_LOW_WATER = 512 * 1024\n\n/** Scrollback retained for a reattaching view (bytes of UTF-8 output). */\nconst DEFAULT_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES = 256 * 1024\n\n/** A detached session is reaped after this long. */\nconst DEFAULT_IDLE_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000\n\n/** An exited session is kept this long for a reattaching view. */\nconst DEFAULT_EXIT_GRACE_MS = 60 * 1000\n\n/** One live terminal session and the sockets currently watching it. */\ninterface HostedTerminal {\n  id: string\n  alias: string\n  shell?: ShellSession\n  sockets: Set<WebSocket>\n  /** Bounded scrollback replayed to an attaching socket. */\n  buffer: string[]\n  bufferBytes: number\n  exited: boolean\n  exit?: { code: number | null; error?: string }\n  /** Pending keyboard-interactive challenge, whoever attached when it arrived. */\n  pendingAuthFinish?: (responses: string[]) => void\n  reapTimer?: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>\n}\n\n/** What the registry needs from the engine (swappable in tests). */\nexport interface TerminalSessionDeps {\n  /** Open one PTY shell for the alias (engine.openShell). */\n  openShell(alias: string, size: { cols: number; rows: number }, onKeyboardInteractive?: KeyboardInteractiveHandler): Promise<ShellSession>\n  /** @returns the current time (defaults to Date.now). */\n  now?: () => number\n  /** Bounded scrollback per session. */\n  maxBufferBytes?: number\n  /** Idle window before a detached session is reaped. */\n  idleMs?: number\n  /** Grace window an exited session is kept for reattaching views. */\n  exitGraceMs?: number\n}\n\n/**\n * The host's terminal session table: open one session per connect, attach any\n * number of sockets, and keep the shell alive across detach.\n */\nexport class TerminalSessionRegistry {\n  private readonly sessions = new Map<string, HostedTerminal>()\n  private readonly deps: TerminalSessionDeps\n  private readonly maxBufferBytes: number\n  private readonly idleMs: number\n  private readonly exitGraceMs: number\n\n  constructor(deps: TerminalSessionDeps) {\n    this.deps = deps\n    this.maxBufferBytes = deps.maxBufferBytes ?? DEFAULT_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES\n    this.idleMs = deps.idleMs ?? DEFAULT_IDLE_MS\n    this.exitGraceMs = deps.exitGraceMs ?? DEFAULT_EXIT_GRACE_MS\n  }\n\n  /** Open a new session for the alias and attach the requesting socket to it. */\n  async open(ws: WebSocket, alias: string, size: { cols: number; rows: number }): Promise<void> {\n    const session: HostedTerminal = {\n      id: randomBytes(9).toString('hex'),\n      alias,\n      sockets: new Set(),\n      buffer: [],\n      bufferBytes: 0,\n      exited: false,\n    }\n    this.sessions.set(session.id, session)\n    this.bind(ws, session)\n    try {\n      const shell = await this.deps.openShell(alias, size, this.keyboardInteractive(session))\n      if (!this.sessions.has(session.id)) {\n        // The session was ended (or the host torn down) while it connected.\n        shell.close()\n        return\n      }\n      session.shell = shell\n      shell.onData = data => { this.pushOutput(session, data.toString('utf8')) }\n      shell.onExit = (code, error) => { this.finish(session, code, error) }\n      this.send(session, { type: 'ready', alias, sessionId: session.id })\n    } catch (error) {\n      this.sessions.delete(session.id)\n      this.send(session, { type: 'exit', code: null, error: error instanceof Error ? null, error: session.exit?.error })\n      // Re-arm the grace window: this socket now holds the exited session open.\n      this.scheduleReap(session, this.exitGraceMs)\n    } else {\n      session.shell?.resize(Math.max(2, size.cols), Math.max(1, size.rows))\n      session.shell?.resume()\n    }\n    return true\n  }\n\n  /** End every session (host teardown, plugin dispose). */\n  dispose(): void {\n    for (const session of [...this.sessions.values()]) this.end(session, false)\n    this.sessions.clear()\n  }\n\n  /** Number of live sessions (introspection for tests and diagnostics). */\n  size(): number {\n    return this.sessions.size\n  }\n\n  /** Wire one socket's frames and lifecycle onto a session. */\n  private bind(ws: WebSocket, session: HostedTerminal): void {\n    session.sockets.add(ws)\n    ws.on('message', (data) => {\n      let frame: { type?: string; data?: string; cols?: number; rows?: number; responses?: string[] }\n      try {\n        frame = JSON.parse(String(data)) as typeof frame\n      } catch {\n        return\n      }\n      if (frame.type === 'input') {\n        session.shell?.send(frame.data ?? '')\n      } else if (frame.type === 'resize') {\n        session.shell?.resize(Math.max(2, frame.cols ?? 80), Math.max(1, frame.rows ?? 24))\n      } else if (frame.type === 'auth_response') {\n        const finish = session.pendingAuthFinish\n        session.pendingAuthFinish = undefined\n        try { finish?.(frame.responses ?? []) } catch { /* the connect already failed */ }\n      } else if (frame.type === 'close') {\n        this.end(session, true)\n      } else if (frame.type === 'detach') {\n        this.detach(ws)\n      }\n    })\n    ws.on('close', () => { this.detach(ws) })\n    ws.on('error', () => { this.detach(ws) })\n  }\n\n  /** Remove a socket from its session, keeping the shell alive. */\n  private detach(ws: WebSocket): void {\n    for (const session of this.sessions.values()) {\n      if (!session.sockets.delete(ws)) continue\n      if (session.sockets.size === 0) {\n        // Nobody is watching: give the view a window to come back before the\n        // remote shell is torn down (or, for an exited one, before its final\n        // screen is dropped).\n        this.scheduleReap(session, session.exited ? this.exitGraceMs : this.idleMs)\n      }\n      return\n    }\n  }\n\n  /** End the session a socket is attached to (explicit close from the view). */\n  private end(session: HostedTerminal, notify: boolean): void {\n    this.clearReap(session)\n    if (this.sessions.delete(session.id) && notify) {\n      if (session.pendingAuthFinish !== undefined) {\n        const finish = session.pendingAuthFinish\n        session.pendingAuthFinish = undefined\n        try { finish([]) } catch { /* the connect already failed */ }\n      }\n    }\n    try { session.shell?.close() } catch { /* channel gone */ }\n  }\n\n  /** Mark a session exited and keep it briefly so a reattaching view sees it. */\n  private finish(session: HostedTerminal, code: number | null, error?: string): void {\n    if (session.exited) return\n    session.exited = true\n    session.exit = { code, error }\n    this.send(session, { type: 'exit', code, error })\n    // The view has its exit frame; close the sockets so neither the browser\n    // nor the host holds a dead transport open. The session record itself\n    // survives the grace window, so a reattach still replays the final screen.\n    for (const ws of [...session.sockets]) {\n      session.sockets.delete(ws)\n      try { ws.close(1000) } catch { /* already closed */ }\n    }\n    this.scheduleReap(session, this.exitGraceMs)\n  }\n\n  /** Append output to the replay buffer, trimmed to the byte cap. */\n  private pushOutput(session: HostedTerminal, data: string): void {\n    session.buffer.push(data)\n    session.bufferBytes += Buffer.byteLength(data)\n    while (session.bufferBytes > this.maxBufferBytes && session.buffer.length > 1) {\n      const dropped = session.buffer.shift()\n      session.bufferBytes -= Buffer.byteLength(dropped ?? '')\n    }\n    this.send(session, { type: 'output', data })\n  }\n\n  /** Broadcast one frame to every attached socket, honoring backpressure. */\n  private send(session: HostedTerminal, frame: TerminalServerFrame): void {\n    for (const ws of session.sockets) this.sendTo(session, ws, frame)\n    this.applyBackpressure(session)\n  }\n\n  private sendTo(session: HostedTerminal, ws: WebSocket, frame: TerminalServerFrame): void {\n    if (ws.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) return\n    try { ws.send(JSON.stringify(frame)) } catch { /* socket raced away */ }\n  }\n\n  /** Pause while any attached socket is backed up;       "content": "/**\n * Wire contract between the host half (routes.ts) and the browser half\n * (client/api.ts).       "content": "/**\n * The /api/dsh-ssh route family: host CRUD, exec, cluster, SFTP transfer\n * (NDJSON progress stream for uploads, binary stream for downloads), remote\n * listing, tunnels, and the WebSocket PTY terminal upgrade. Every route\n * carries a loopback-only trust fence (plus browser same-origin markers) —\n * these endpoints execute commands on remote servers, so LAN-exposed dsh web\n * deployments must not serve them.\n */\n\nimport { closeSync, createReadStream, createWriteStream, mkdirSync, openSync } from 'node:fs'\nimport { unlink } from 'node:fs/promises'\nimport type { IncomingMessage, ServerResponse } from 'node:http'\nimport { basename, join } from 'node:path'\nimport { tmpdir } from 'node:os'\nimport { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto'\nimport { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from 'ws'\nimport type { WebRoute, WebUpgradeRoute } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver'\nimport type { SshEngine } from './engine.ts'\nimport { TerminalSessionRegistry } from './engine/terminal-sessions.ts'\nimport { readJsonBody, writeJson } from './http.ts'\nimport { isLoopbackRequest } from './loopback.ts'\nimport { SSH_API, type HostPayload, type TerminalServerFrame } from './protocol.ts'\nimport type { HostStore } from './store.ts'\n\n/** Cap on declared upload bodies (staged to disk before SFTP). */\nconst MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024\n\n/**\n * One noServer WebSocket server for terminal upgrades: the browser half uses\n * a standards-compliant WebSocket, so the host must speak real RFC 6455\n * frames (the webserver hands us the raw upgraded socket).\n */\nconst terminalWss = new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })\n\n/** URL query helper (first value, decoded). */\nfunction queryParam(url: URL, name: string): string | undefined {\n  const value = url.searchParams.get(name)\n  return value === null ? undefined : value\n}\n\n/** Route family dependencies. */\nexport interface SshRoutesDeps {\n  /** The host store (CRUD). */\n  store: HostStore\n  /** The engine (ops). */\n  engine: SshEngine\n  /** Temp dir for upload/download staging (tests inject a sandbox). */\n  stagingDir?: string\n/** Upload byte cap override (tests); defaults to MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES. */\nmaxUploadBytes?: number\n}\n\n/**\n * Build every /api/dsh-ssh route (exact paths) plus the terminal upgrade.\n * @param deps - store, engine, staging dir.\n * @returns routes and the upgrade route.\n */\nexport function makeRoutes(deps: SshRoutesDeps): { routes: WebRoute[]; upgrade: WebUpgradeRoute; terminalSessions: TerminalSessionRegistry } {\n  const { store, engine } = deps\n  const staging = deps.stagingDir ?? join(tmpdir(), 'dsh-ssh-uploads')\nconst maxUploadBytes = deps.maxUploadBytes ?? MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES\n  // The upload route stages request bodies here; it must exist before the\n  // first request (a missing dir would hang the first upload forever).\n  // 0700 keeps in-flight transfers unreadable to other local users (the\n  // staged files below are 0600; downloads are pre-created 0600 as well).\n  mkdirSync(staging, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })\n\n  /** Guard helper: fence + method check. */\n  const guard = (req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse, method: string): boolean => {\n    if (!isLoopbackRequest(req)) {\n      writeJson(res, 403, { error: 'forbidden: loopback-only' })\n      return false\n    }\n    if (req.method !== method) {\n      writeJson(res, 405, { error: `method not allowed: ${req.method}` })\n      return false\n    }\n    return true\n  }\n\n  const routes: WebRoute[] = [\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------ hosts\n    {\n      kind: 'exact',\n      path: SSH_API.hosts,\n      handler: async (req, res) => {\n        // One handler per path (the webserver keyed route registry rejects\n        // duplicate (kind, path)); dispatch by HTTP method here.\n        const method = req.method ?? 'GET'\n        if (!isLoopbackRequest(req)) {\n          writeJson(res, 403, { error: 'forbidden: loopback-only' })\n          return\n        }\n        const url = new URL(req.url ?? '/', 'http://localhost')\n        if (method === 'GET') {\n          writeJson(res, 200, { hosts: engine.list(queryParam(url, 'query')) })\n          return\n        }\n        if (method === 'POST') {\n          const body = (await readJsonBody(req)) as Record<string, unknown> | null\n          if (body === null) {\n            writeJson(res, 400, { error: 'invalid JSON body' })\n            return\n          }\n          try {\n            const entry = store.create(body as unknown as HostPayload)\n            writeJson(res, 201, { host: store.summarize(entry) })\n          } catch (error) {\n            writeJson(res, 400, { error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })\n          }\n          return\n        }\n        if (method !== 'PATCH' && method !== 'DELETE') {\n          writeJson(res, 405, { error: `method not allowed: ${method}` })\n          return\n        }\n        const alias = queryParam(url, 'alias')\n        if (alias === undefined || alias === '') {\n          writeJson(res, 400, { error: 'alias query parameter is required' })\n          return\n        }\n        if (method === 'PATCH') {\n          const body = (await readJsonBody(req)) as Record<string, unknown> | null\n          if (body === null) {\n            writeJson(res, 400, { error: 'invalid JSON body' })\n            return\n          }\n          try {\n            const entry = store.update(alias, body as unknown as Partial<HostPayload>)\n            // Connection-relevant changes invalidate the pooled connection:\n            // without this the pool would keep running commands on the old\n            // host/credentials until the idle sweep (up to 30 min later).\n            // Agent forwarding belongs here too: it is fixed per connection\n            // (ssh2 negotiates it when the channel opens), so toggling it must\n            // reconnect or the new setting silently never takes effect.\n            const patch = body as Record<string, unknown>\n            if (['host', 'port', 'user', 'auth', 'proxyJump', 'proxyCommand', 'forwardAgent'].some(key => patch[key] !== undefined)) {\n              engine.dropAlias(alias)\n            }\n            writeJson(res, 200, { host: store.summarize(entry) })\n          } catch (error) {\n            writeJson(res, 400, { error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })\n          }\n          return\n        }\n        if (method === 'DELETE') {\n          try {\n            engine.dropAlias(alias)\n            store.delete(alias)\n            writeJson(res, 200, { ok: true })\n          } catch (error) {\n            writeJson(res, 400, { error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })\n          }\n          return\n        }\n        writeJson(res, 405, { error: `method not allowed: ${method}` })\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      kind: 'exact',\n      path: SSH_API.importSshConfig,\n      handler: async (req, res) => {\n        if (!guard(req, res, 'POST')) return\n        try {\n          writeJson(res, 200, { result: store.importFromSshConfig() })\n        } catch (error) {\n          writeJson(res, 500, { error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------ ops\n    {\n      kind: 'exact',\n      path: SSH_API.test,\n      handler: async (req, res) => {\n        if (!guard(req, res, 'POST')) return\n        const body = (await readJsonBody(req)) as Record<string, unknown> | null\n        const alias = typeof body?.alias === 'string' ? body.alias : ''\n        if (alias === '') {\n          writeJson(res, 400, { error: 'alias is required' })\n          return\n        }\n        try {\n          writeJson(res, 200, { result: await engine.test(alias) })\n        } catch (error) {\n          writeJson(res, 500, { error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      kind: 'exact',\n      path: SSH_API.exec,\n      handler: async (req, res) => {\n        if (!guard(req, res, 'POST')) return\n        const body = (await readJsonBody(req)) as Record<string, unknown> | null\n        const alias = typeof body?.alias === 'string' ? body.alias : ''\n        const command = typeof body?.command === 'string' ? body.command : ''\n        if (alias === '' || command === '') {\n          writeJson(res, 400, { error: 'alias and command are required' })\n          return\n        }\n        const timeoutMs = typeof body?.timeoutMs === 'number' ? body.timeoutMs : undefined\n        try {\n          writeJson(res, 200, { result: await engine.exec(alias, command, timeoutMs) })\n        } catch (error) {\n          writeJson(res, 500, { error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      kind: 'exact',\n      path: SSH_API.cluster,\n      handler: async (req, res) => {\n        if (!guard(req, res, 'POST')) return\n        const body = (await readJsonBody(req)) as Record<string, unknown> | null\n        const command = typeof body?.command === 'string' ? body.command : ''\n        if (command === '') {\n          writeJson(res, 400, { error: 'command is required' })\n          return\n        }\n        const aliases = Array.isArray(body?.aliases) ? body.aliases.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === 'string') : undefined\n        const tags = Array.isArray(body?.tags) ? body.tags.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === 'string') : undefined\n        const environment = typeof body?.environment === 'string' ? body.environment : undefined\n        const timeoutMs = typeof body?.timeoutMs === 'number' ? body.timeoutMs : undefined\n        const maxWorkers = typeof body?.maxWorkers === 'number' ? body.maxWorkers : undefined\n        const hasAliases = aliases?.some(alias => alias.trim() !== '') === true\n        const hasEnvironment = typeof environment === 'string' && environment.trim() !== ''\n        const hasTags = tags?.some(tag => tag.trim() !== '') === true\n        if (!hasAliases && !hasEnvironment && !hasTags) {\n          writeJson(res, 400, { error: 'ssh_cluster requires aliases, environment, or tags to limit the target set' })\n          return\n        }\n        try {\n          writeJson(res, 200, { results: await engine.cluster({ command, aliases, environment, tags, timeoutMs, maxWorkers }) })\n        } catch (error) {\n          writeJson(res, 500, { error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- ls\n    {\n      kind: 'exact',\n      path: SSH_API.ls,\n      handler: async (req, res) => {\n        if (!guard(req, res, 'GET')) return\n        const url = new URL(req.url ?? '/', 'http://localhost')\n        const alias = queryParam(url, 'alias')\n        const path = queryParam(url, 'path') ?? '/'\n        if (alias === undefined || alias === '') {\n          writeJson(res, 400, { error: 'alias query parameter is required' })\n          return\n        }\n        try {\n          writeJson(res, 200, { entries: await engine.ls(alias, path) })\n        } catch (error) {\n          writeJson(res, 400, { error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    // --------------------------------------------------------- tunnel\n    {\n      kind: 'exact',\n      path: SSH_API.tunnel,\n      handler: async (req, res) => {\n        if (!guard(req, res, 'POST')) return\n        const body = (await readJsonBody(req)) as Record<string, unknown> | null\n        const action = typeof body?.action === 'string' ? body.action : ''\n        if (action === 'list') {\n          writeJson(res, 200, { tunnels: engine.listTunnels() })\n          return\n        }\n        if (action === 'start') {\n          const alias = typeof body?.alias === 'string' ? body.alias : ''\n          const remotePort = typeof body?.remotePort === 'number' ? body.remotePort : undefined\n          if (alias === '' || remotePort === undefined) {\n            writeJson(res, 400, { error: 'alias and remotePort are required' })\n            return\n          }\n          try {\n            const tunnel = await engine.startTunnel(alias, {\n              remotePort,\n              remoteHost: typeof body?.remoteHost === 'string' && body.remoteHost !== '' ? body.remoteHost : undefined,\n              localPort: typeof body?.localPort === 'number' ? body.localPort : undefined,\n            })\n            writeJson(res, 200, { tunnel })\n          } catch (error) {\n            writeJson(res, 500, { error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })\n          }\n          return\n        }\n        if (action === 'stop') {\n          const id = typeof body?.tunnelId === 'string' ? body.tunnelId : ''\n          if (id === '') {\n            writeJson(res, 400, { error: 'tunnelId is required' })\n            return\n          }\n          writeJson(res, 200, { ok: engine.stopTunnel(id) })\n          return\n        }\n        if (action === 'stop-all') {\n          const alias = typeof body?.alias === 'string' ? body.alias : undefined\n          writeJson(res, 200, { stopped: engine.stopAllTunnels(alias === '' ? undefined : alias) })\n          return\n        }\n        writeJson(res, 400, { error: `unknown action '${action}'` })\n      },\n    },\n    // --------------------------------------------------------- upload\n    {\n      kind: 'exact',\n      path: SSH_API.upload,\n      handler: async (req, res) => {\n        if (!guard(req, res, 'POST')) return\n        const url = new URL(req.url ?? '/', 'http://localhost')\n        const alias = queryParam(url, 'alias')\n        const remotePath = queryParam(url, 'remotePath')\n        if (alias === undefined || remotePath === undefined) {\n          writeJson(res, 400, { error: 'alias and remotePath query parameters are required' })\n          return\n        }\n        const declared = Number(req.headers['content-length'])\n        if (Number.isFinite(declared) && declared > maxUploadBytes) {\n          writeJson(res, 413, { error: 'upload body too large' })\n          return\n        }\n        res.writeHead(200, {\n          'content-type': 'application/x-ndjson; charset=utf-8',\n          'cache-control': 'no-cache',\n          'referrer-policy': 'no-referrer',\n        })\n        const emit = (line: unknown): void => {\n          try { res.write(JSON.stringify(line) + '\\n') } catch { /* client gone */ }\n        }\n        // Stage the uploaded bytes, then SFTP them out with progress frames.\n        const tmp = join(staging, `upload-${randomBytes(6).toString('hex')}`)\n        const sink = createWriteStream(tmp, { mode: 0o600 })\n        let settled = false\n        // Every terminal path (sink error, client abort, response loss) must\n        // emit a result frame, end the response, and remove the tmp file.\n        const fail = (error: unknown): void => {\n          if (settled) return\n          settled = true\n          emit({ type: 'result', ok: false, error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })\n          // End the response only after the tmp file is gone, and unlink only\n          // after the sink is fully closed: destroying a WriteStream whose\n          // fs.open is still pending lets the open RE-CREATE the file after\n          // an early unlink, leaving staging populated (this raced the\n          // response end and made the byte-cap test flaky).\n          const cleanup = (): void => {\n            void unlink(tmp).catch(() => undefined).finally(() => {\n              try { res.end() } catch { /* closed */ }\n            })\n          }\n          if (sink.destroyed) {\n            cleanup()\n          } else {\n            sink.once('close', cleanup)\n            try { sink.destroy() } catch { cleanup() }\n          }\n        }\n        const done = (): void => {\n          if (settled) return\n          settled = true\n          try { res.end() } catch { /* closed */ }\n        }\n        sink.on('error', (error) => fail(error))\n        req.on('error', (error) => fail(error))\n        req.on('aborted', () => fail('upload aborted by the client'))\n        res.on('error', () => fail('response stream closed'))\n        res.on('close', () => { if (!res.writableEnded) fail('connection closed') })\n        // The content-length pre-check above can be bypassed by chunked or\n        // header-less requests: count the bytes as they actually arrive and\n        // abort the moment the cap is exceeded.\n        let received = 0\n        let capped = false\n        req.on('data', (chunk: Buffer) => {\n          received += chunk.byteLength\n          if (received > maxUploadBytes && !capped) {\n            capped = true\n            fail('upload body too large')\n            // Keep the socket alive until the response flush finishes:\n            // destroying the request here races res.end() and the client\n            // sees a hang-up instead of the result frame. Drain the rest of\n            // the body so the socket can close cleanly afterwards.\n            res.on('finish', () => { try { req.destroy() } catch { /* closed */ } })\n            req.resume()\n          }\n        })\n        req.pipe(sink)\n        sink.on('finish', async () => {\n          if (settled) return\n          emit({ type: 'progress', progress: { phase: 'connecting', file: remotePath, transferred: 0, total: 0, percent: 0 } })\n          try {\n            const outcome = await engine.upload(alias, tmp, remotePath, false, progress => emit({ type: 'progress', progress }))\n            emit({ type: 'result', ok: true, transferredBytes: outcome.bytes })\n          } catch (error) {\n            emit({ type: 'result', ok: false, error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })\n          } finally {\n            await unlink(tmp).catch(() => undefined)\n            done()\n          }\n        })\n      },\n    },\n    // ------------------------------------------------------- download\n    {\n      kind: 'exact',\n      path: SSH_API.download,\n      handler: async (req, res) => {\n        if (!guard(req, res, 'GET')) return\n        const url = new URL(req.url ?? '/', 'http://localhost')\n        const alias = queryParam(url, 'alias')\n        const remotePath = queryParam(url, 'remotePath')\n        if (alias === undefined || remotePath === undefined) {\n          writeJson(res, 400, { error: 'alias and remotePath query parameters are required' })\n          return\n        }\n        const tmp = join(staging, `download-${randomBytes(6).toString('hex')}`)\n        try {\n          // Pre-create with 0600: ssh2's fastGet opens the destination with\n          // umask-default permissions and a pre-created file keeps the mode.\n          closeSync(openSync(tmp, 'w', 0o600))\n          const outcome = await engine.download(alias, remotePath, tmp)\n          res.writeHead(200, {\n            'content-type': 'application/octet-stream',\n            'content-length': String(outcome.bytes),\n            'content-disposition': `attachment; filename=\"${basename(remotePath).replace(/\"/g, '')}\"`,\n            'referrer-policy': 'no-referrer',\n          })\n          await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n            const source = createReadStream(tmp)\n            source.on('error', reject)\n            res.on('error', reject)\n            source.pipe(res)\n            source.on('end', resolve)\n          })\n        } catch (error) {\n          if (!res.headersSent) {\n            writeJson(res, 400, { error: error instanceof Error ? '/', 'http://localhost')\n      const alias = queryParam(url, 'alias')\n      const sessionId = queryParam(url, 'session')\n      if (alias === undefined && sessionId === undefined) {\n        socket.write('HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n')\n        socket.destroy()\n        return\n      }\n      const cols = Number.parseInt(queryParam(url, 'cols') ?? '80', 10)\n      const rows = Number.parseInt(queryParam(url, 'rows') ?? '24', 10)\n      const size = {\n        cols: Number.isFinite(cols) ? cols : 80,\n        rows: Number.isFinite(rows) ? rows : 24,\n      }\n      terminalWss.handleUpgrade(req, socket, head, (ws) => {\n        if (sessionId !== undefined) {\n          if (terminalSessions.attach(ws, sessionId, size)) return\n          // The session was reaped or the host restarted: tell the view so it\n          // can fall back to a fresh connect instead of sitting blank.\n          const expired: TerminalServerFrame = { type: 'exit', code: null, error: 'terminal session expired' }\n          try { ws.send(JSON.stringify(expired)) } catch { /* socket raced away */ }\n          try { ws.close(1000) } catch { /* already closed */ }\n          return\n        }\n        void terminalSessions.open(ws, alias as string, size)\n      })\n    },\n  }\n\n  return { routes, upgrade, terminalSessions }\n}\n"
